Three football confederations rebuke Infantino, say sport ‘belongs to no individual’. FIFA President Gianni Infantino came under renewed fire on Monday as a joint letter from three confederations — European football’s governing body UEFA, Confederations of North America, Central America and the Caribbean (CONCACAF) and Asia (AFC) — declared football “belongs to no individual”. Infantino has been the butt of scathing criticism ever since launching, and then withdrawing within days, a plan to bring private investment into FIFA competitions, including World Cups. FIFA had hit back on Saturday at “a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine” football’s governing body and Infantino. However, Monday’s letter from UEFA, CONCACAF and AFC showed his critics are unbowed. “Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held,” they wrote. “When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with authority, that duty has been abandoned,” the confederations added. The three confederations had been vociferous in their condemnation of Infantino’s plan and had not let up after it was shelved. CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is viewed as a potential challenger to Infantino, who will seek a fourth and final term at the FIFA presidential election in Rabat next March. Candidates have to be declared by November 18. UEFA’s threat to boycott World Cups if the private investment plan went ahead — in theory depriving the competition of teams including reigning men’s champions Spain and 2026 semi-finalists France and England — proved pivotal in Infantino withdrawing his plan. Prior to this debacle, Infantino had looked likely to be unopposed, after overseeing a successful World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada. The 56-year-old Swiss, who has been in situ for 10 years, has received the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) while South American governing body CONMEBOL are largely supportive. The confederations do not vote as blocs and there have been some supportive voices for Infantino from CONCACAF, Mexico and two AFC members — Kuwait and 2022 World Cup hosts Qatar, where he has a house. Although the proposal has been dead in the water for over a week now — UEFA had termed it “a shabby, opaque, backroom deal” — the confederations harangued him for a lack of judgment. “FIFA’s recent letter to its Vice-Presidents and 211 Member Associations acknowledges that mistakes were made in the process,” they said. “It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment.” ‘Accountability’ Although Infantino had received the “full support” of senior FIFA directors last week in an emergency meeting he called in Morocco, the confederations said it was meaningless. “This recent meeting, where a select number of members of the FIFA Management Committee — not the full Committee — were summoned abroad, rather than leadership going to Zurich to address the heart of FIFA, its staff, only reinforces these concerns and represents a continuation of the very pattern of conduct that brought us to this moment,” they said. “It is not the conduct of a custodian of the game, but of one who believes the game is answerable to him.” Infantino had been basking in the afterglow of a hugely successful World Cup — the largest ever involving 48 teams. However, the confederations made clear in the letter that it was not just Infantino who had made this possible. “The growth over the past decade has been real,” they said. “But that progress was never the work of one individual. “It was the product of FIFA, the Confederations, the Member Associations, and the thousands of people who dedicate their lives to the game. “The expanded tournaments, the awarding of the 2030 and 2034 FIFA World Cups, the distribution of resources to associations. These were shared achievements, agreed together, delivered together.” The confederations signed off their letter by claiming that under Infantino’s leadership “there is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness”. They added: “That is why we have taken this stance: not lightly and not alone, but together, and out of duty to the game we serve. Football’s strength has always been its unity.”

In letter to PM, Achakzai urges 'immediate' appointment of new chief election commissioner. In a letter to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai on Monday urged the appointment of a new chief election commissioner of the Election Commission of Pakistan, as well as two members representing Sindh and Balochistan. In the letter, dated August 10 and available with Dawn , Achakzai, who heads the Tehreek Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) and is chairman of the Pakhtunkhwa Milli Awami Party, drew the prime minister’s attention to a “critical constitutional duty” and stated that the statutory tenure of the CEC and the members representing Sindh and Balochistan had ended on January 26, 2025. To that effect, he urged the “immediate filling” of the offices, terming it “essential for maintaining the operational continuity, independence, and credibility of the commission”. In his letter, Achakzai cited two provisions of the Constitution, including Article 213(2A), which he said “mandates that the prime minister shall, in consultation with the leader of the opposition in the NA, forward three names for the appointment of the CEC to a Parliamentary Committee for hearing and confirmation”. Article 218(2)(b), meanwhile, required that the “appointment of the members of the ECP from each province shall follow the exact same procedural requirement of consultation between the prime minister and the leader of the opposition under Article 213”. Achakzai also drew attention to the matter at a meeting of the TTAP on Monday and informed the participants about the letter, according to a post on TTAP’s X account. “The meeting expressed astonishment and concern over the fact that the current CEC and members continue to serve even after the expiry of their constitutional terms, and that the prime minister has not yet initiated the constitutional process for appointing new members.” The meeting termed the establishment of an “impartial and independent EC essential for fair, transparent, and free elections”. “Therefore, the prime minister should immediately meet with the opposition leader in this regard and initiate this important constitutional process without delay,” it added. The incumbent CEC Sikandar Sultan Raja, along with Sindh and Balochistan ECP members, have now been in office for over a year after the expiry of their constitutionally mandated five-year terms. The terms of the three officials ended on Jan 26, 2025. Under Article 215(4) of the Constitution, appointments to these posts were required within 45 days after the positions became vacant , i.e., by March 12, 2025. However, a proviso inserted into Article 215(1) through the 26th Constitutional Amendment allows the CEC and members to continue until their successors are appointed. The incumbent CEC and two ECP members are serving under this provision. At the time, the delay was partly attributed to the absence of an officially notified leader of the opposition in the NA. It should also be mentioned that on July 30, the ECP had refused to recognise Achakzai as chairman of the PkMAP over the party’s failure to hold intra-party elections.

Iran says Pak-Saudi-Turkiye deal shows 'change in perception' towards US. Iran’s foreign ministry said on Monday that the defence pact signed last week between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye was “a sign of a change in the perception” of regional countries towards the United States. The joint defence agreement, signed in Makkah on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. “This development is a sign of a change in the perception of the countries of the region,” ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said while responding to a query during a weekly press briefing on Monday. “Considering the developments of the last two to three years, the countries of the region have realised that security is not a commodity that can be bought from false security brokers,” Iran’s state media quoted him as saying, referring to the United States. Baqaei further said that there was “no reason to worry that this treaty will be against Iran”, highlighting Iran’s deep religious, historical and civilisational ties with Pakistan, Turkiye and even Saudi Arabia. “This development is an important sign that the countries of the region have concluded that they cannot rely on and trust the claim of security provided by the United States and some other actors outside the region, and they are attempting to try another method; by relying on their own capabilities and perspectives,” IRNA quoted Baqaei as saying. “Any plan that is based on the geopolitical and historical realities of the region, is comprehensive and inclusive, and correctly identifies the enemy and the threat, has a chance of helping to strengthen security and prevent instability and abuses by the Zionist enemy and its allies,” he added, referring to Israel. In response to a question about Iran’s willingness to possibly join the joint pact, Baqaei said Iran has always “emphasised pursuing security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries” and “free from the influence and destructive intervention” of foreign actors. “Those plans still exist and can certainly be updated in light of developments,” the spokesperson added. “We are in close contact with neighbouring countries and regional countries, and we hope that all countries will learn from the developments of the last two or three years and adopt the best path to strengthen the region’s collective security,” he said, according to IRNA . Asked about Pakistan’s invitations to Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to visit Pakistan, Baqaei said, “This visit will take place whenever the time is right. Bilateral relations are mainly considered.” He added: “The relationship between Iran and Pakistan is a very important one. In the last seven or eight months, it has become even more important than before, for various reasons.” Pact aimed at regional peace, Dar tells Iran FM Later in the day, Deputy Prime Minister and FM Ishaq Dar “shared the contours” of the pact with Iran’s Araghchi in a phone call, the Foreign Office (FO) said. Dar underscored its “objectives of strengthening strategic cooperation and contributing to regional peace and security”. FM Araghchi thanked his Pakistani counterpart for “sharing the key aspects of the agreement”, FO said. The two leaders also “exchanged views on regional and international developments, with particular focus on the evolving situation in the region and efforts to promote peace and stability”. On Sunday, DPM Dar said that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement remained “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles after the Turkish foreign minister said Egypt could be joining the pact. Dar said the pact was the “culmination of years of discussions and coordination”, adding that it was “purely defensive” in nature. “It is not targeted against any country and its sole purpose is to further strengthen our ongoing efforts towards peace, stability and prosperity in the wider region.” The deputy PM clarified that the pact did not abrogate or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between the signatory countries, or with other countries or organisations. Dar speaks with Kuwait FM, others on pact Separately, Kuwait’s Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah felicitated Dar on the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the FO said. The two dignitaries spoke late on Sunday and also “exchanged views on the regional situation, including occupied East Jerusalem”. They also discussed bilateral relations between the two countries and “matters of mutual interest, including the follow-up to FM Jarrah’s recent visit to Pakistan and further enhancing cooperation and investment in key sectors”. “The two sides agreed to remain closely engaged,” the FO added. The deputy premier also shared the contours of the pact with Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi and former Guinea-Bissau president General Umaro Sissoco Embaló. In a joint call with them late last night, Dar shared the agreement’s “significance for strengthening strategic cooperation and contributing to regional peace, stability and security”, FO said. Dar and Tshisekedi also exchanged views on Pakistan-DRC relations and agreed on the importance of further strengthening bilateral cooperation, including through high-level exchanges. DPM Dar had also spoken to Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand a day ago. “The two exchanged views on the regional situation, including the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye,” the FO said. It added that Dar shared the “essence of the agreement” and the “joint resolve of the three countries to contribute to regional peace, stability and security”.

Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact ‘entirely for defensive purposes’, not aggression: PM Shehbaz. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday affirmed that the recently signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression. The joint defence agreement, signed on August 7 between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them. Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz recalled that he, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the pact in Makkah on Friday. The prime minister stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”. “Its purpose is definitely not that any aggression occurs. It is entirely for defensive purposes, for peace, tranquillity and progress in the region,” he affirmed. “I believe this agreement is a source of strength not just among these three countries, but for the entire Muslim ummah,” he noted. PM Shehbaz particularly felicitated Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar as well as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir on the signing of the agreement. Efforts for the joint defence pact had been underway for “many years and materialised this Friday”, the prime minister said. He noted that while Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already entered the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in September 2025, Islamabad and Ankara also had “arrangements for decades” between them. PM Shehbaz recalled that the Pakistani nation and the army had been honoured to “defend the world’s holiest places” of Makkah and Madina for years along with the Saudi forces. “Last year, with Allah’s grace, this arrangement was officially recognised so that a proper agreement was signed. Friday’s agreement is another extension of it, with a trilateral agreement signed.” In a statement issued by the Foreign Office earlier in the day, Dar felicitated the nation on the agreement’s signing. He reiterated his comments from Sunday wherein he said the pact was defensive in nature and not directed against any country. Dar also noted that the term of treating an attack on one of them as an attack against all three was “consistent with the inherent right of individual and collective self-defence under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter”. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”. Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”. ‘Once in power, AJK govt will offer dialogue to those willing’ Speaking on Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), PM Shehbaz favoured dialogue with protesters who have been at odds with the authorities over the 12 seats reserved for refugees and other issues, leading to a tense situation in the region for the past two months. He said that once the new government comes to power in AJK — with PML-N already claiming a two-thirds majority — the matter of continuing talks with the protesters “will progress”. The prime minister declared that those “who only want to cause anarchy will not be allowed to do so, but those who want to peacefully and patiently discuss the situation, the new government will provide a chance for that”. “In any respected society, no permission can be given for lawlessness. If there is any demand or any matters, they should be resolved through talks at a table,” he said. PM Shehbaz went on to say that the government had “clear evidence that those who purposefully worsened the situation there were working on the directives of the enemy”. He recalled that despite that, the government had held a multi-party conference in Muzaffarabad before the elections, with only one political party being absent — apparently referring to the PTI which has boycotted the polls. “Every aspect was discussed there, and […] those who wanted refugee seats to be changed, reduced or abolished were advised to let the elections go on as planned and bring forward their case in the new assembly,” he said, adding that this would resolve the matter as per the constitution of AJK. “All matters were settled, but they remained adamant on this and needlessly insisted, which unfortunately worsened the situation,” the prime minister said. Speaking about the ongoing elections in AJK, PM Shehbaz asserted that Kashmiris have “overwhelmingly voted” for his PML-N. The PML-N has so far bagged 24 seats out of a total 45 — nine from Mirpur polls held on July 27 and 15 in the second phase comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. The third phase of elections in Poonch Division began today . The prime minister noted that based on the results from Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions, along with the seats reserved for refugees from India-held Kashmir, the PML-N has “almost established a majority”. “This vote is a vote of trust in Mian Nawaz Sharif and for his leadership. I am hopeful that once we set up a government there, under his leadership, AJK will once again set out on the journey to progress and prosperity,” he said, thanking those who voted for his party. ‘Terrorists being annihilated day and night’ At the federal cabinet meeting, PM Shehbaz also touched upon the issue of terrorism in the country and mentioned the lives lost in recent terrorist attacks. He noted that terrorists escalated their activities in “some areas of Pakistan in the past few days”. The premier recalled the August 2 Swat suicide bombing that claimed 17 lives and the martyrdom of Deputy Superintendent of Police Diyar Khan in an attack on a Hangu police checkpost. He paid tribute to the sacrifices of the personnel, including Captain Hamza Akram and Major Hafiz Ihsan Elahi, who were martyred during operations in Hangu and North Waziristan , respectively. The prime minister affirmed that “ Fitna Al Khawarij are being annihilated day and night”, referring to terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). “These sacrifices will not go in vain and will bear fruition. One day will come when Pakistan will once again be free from terrorism and will move rapidly towards peace and progress,” PM Shehbaz said. The prime minister also expressed his condolences over the death of PML-N MNA Malik Muhammad Iqbal Channar, describing him as a “longtime friend”. “He was a person who was a supporter in bad times,” he said, adding that he and PML-N President Nawaz Sharif knew Channar since 1985. The cabinet also prayed for the elevated ranks of the martyrs and Channar.

Police in India's Jharkhand fire tear gas, use batons to disperse youth protesters. Police in eastern India used tear gas, batons and water cannon to disperse thousands of youth protesters as they marched on the state legislature in Jharkhand state on Monday over alleged wrongdoing in civil service examinations, TV footage showed. Students and unemployed youth in Jharkhand, one of India’s poorer states, launched the protests late last month over the alleged wrongdoing, including recruitment test paper leaks. The protest follows weeks-long youth-led demonstrations in the capital, Delhi, also linked to exam paper leaks , which led to the resignation of the country’s Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan last month. Police and paramilitary forces used tear gas , pellet guns and batons in Delhi to scatter some 50,000 youth protesters, some of whom clashed with police. The demonstrations were seen as a reflection of their anger over corruption in education, a lack of opportunities and unemployment. The demands of protesters in Jharkhand include an overhaul of the state’s examination system, cancellation of some tests and an investigation by the federal police. At least six protesters were on hunger strike, including student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, 33, who has been fasting for more than a week. “We want the whole system to change,” Mahto said, as quoted by Indian media, demanding an end to the use of a private company that conducts tests for state civil service. The protest began on July 25 and intensified after thousands gathered at a stadium in the state capital, Ranchi. On Monday, they marched on the state legislature, climbing over police barricades, holding placards, waving the national flag and shouting slogans, amid high security. Some pushed against barricades and scuffled with police, who responded by firing tear gas rounds, using water cannon and beating them with batons, TV footage showed. Police said they had to use mild force after some protesters became violent. “We showed minimal aggression for a really short time because they are just students,” Ranchi city police chief Paras Rana told ANI news agency. “I appeal to everyone to be peaceful and not be violent. Your demands are reaching the government; do not show aggression.” The state government ruled by a regional party opposed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi has held talks with the protesters. It said a majority of their demands had been accepted and that it was open to more talks. Additional input from AFP

Peshawar High Court grants transit bail to Noreen Niazi in Peca case. PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Monday granted transit bail to Noreen Niazi, the sister of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, in a case registered under the Peca Act 2016, directing her to appear before the relevant Islamabad court on or before August 20. In July, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) registered a case against Noreen, accusing her of passing derogatory and inflammatory remarks against state institutions during a podcast interview and in subsequent clips shared on X. A single-member PHC bench comprising Justice Arshad Ali heard Noreen’s petition, represented by a panel of lawyers, including Ali Zaman, Amir Zeb and Barrister Sarwar Muzaffar Shah In its order issued on Monday, the bench stated that the petitioner had approached the court seeking transit bail in connection with a first information report (FIR) registered against her at the NCCIA police station in Islamabad on July 27 under various provisions of the Peca Act 2016 and the Pakistan Penal Code, enabling her to approach the competent court. The order noted that the petitioner had claimed to have been falsely implicated in the case and that, except for the bare allegations contained in the FIR, there was no other cogent evidence on record to connect her with the alleged offence. “In the circumstances of the case, the petitioner’s request, being reasonable, merits consideration,” the order noted, adding that “consequently this application is accepted and the accused petitioner is granted ad-interim transit pre-arrest bail provided she furnishes bail bonds in the sum of Rs80,000 with two sureties,” it said. The bench also directed the petitioner to approach the competent forum in Islamabad for bail on or before August 20, as the PHC order would be effective till that day. Meanwhile, the counsels for the petitioner argued that their client was innocent and falsely implicated in the case registered at the NCCIA police station. They said the local police were trying to arrest their client with mala fide intentions, to humiliate and unjustly harass her for some ulterior motive. The counsels also said the allegations contained in the FIR were false and politically motivated, and were based on an erroneous interpretation of statements allegedly attributed to their client. Talking to reporters after the hearing, Noreen said she came to know about the NCCIA case against her after arriving in Peshawar. “I did speak inside in my house, which I do not have recollection of, and someone got that to them and they made a case against me,” she claimed. Noreen further alleged that cases had been lodged against her other sisters and that now one had been registered against her as well. “Too many cases are being registered across Pakistan, and no one knows why they have been lodged. The case against me is the same,” she said. In response to a question, she said they had never been to Peshawar, so the question of their interfering in KP affairs did not even arise. Earlier, the Lahore High Court had also granted her an interim protective bail, directing her to approach a relevant Islamabad court. Before registering an FIR, the NCCIA had summoned Noreen to appear before it on July 20 over allegations of disseminating “false, offensive and inflammatory” content against state institutions. While the notice did not specify the content in relation to which Noreen has been summoned, it was issued after the clip of her making claims in relation to last year’s brief military conflict between Pakistan and India was widely shared on social media. In the clip, she is seen alleging during an interview that the conflict was “orchestrated” to improve the image of Pakistan’s military. She claimed the “drama” was played out in collaboration with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, questioning why Modi would have refrained from further attacking Pakistan otherwise. In this connection, she went on to allege that the objective was to get Israel recognised by Pakistan, linking US President Donald Trump’s praise of Pakistan’s leadership with Israel’s recognition as well.

PTI leadership, TTAP on board for September 27 long march to Islamabad: Sohail Afridi. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday said PTI’s political leadership and its ally, the Tehreek Tahaffuz-i-Ayeen Pakistan (TTAP), were on board with the call for a long march to Islamabad on September 27. Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’, CM Afridi said, “The PTI’s political leadership across the country and its ally, the TTAP, are all on board with the long march, and they collectively agreed on September 27 as the date for it.” Responding to a question about Imran Khan’s sister Aleema Khan’s reservations over the date, he said she was a “non-political individual” and would agree to the date once the PTI apprised her of all the facts and figures. CM Afridi also denied allegations by a PTI member currently residing outside Pakistan that he had met Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi before finalising the date for the long march. “That allegation was rubbish. At the time of the alleged meeting, I was at KP House in Islamabad, contrary to the claim that I had met him in Peshawar,” he said. In response to a question, CM Afridi also rejected the impression of a communication gap between the party’s leadership and workers. Talking about the ‘D-Chowk, D-Chowk’ slogans during the recent Peshawar rally , he said institutions that were not granting political space to the PTI should understand that the party’s leadership had taken on a great burden by seeking to resolve issues through mutual understanding. “However, not just in KP but across Pakistan, particularly the youth, no one will be able to contain them when they come out on Sept 27, because I can see passion and a ray of light in their eyes,” the chief minister said. During the interview, the KP chief minister also criticised the federal government led by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for economic inefficiency and bad governance. He said that if he met the PTI founder at Adiala jail and was instructed to defer the Sept 27 date for the long march, he would agree. CM Afridi added that he would also follow Imran’s instructions if asked to pave the way for talks. At the outset of his interview, Afridi said the PTI had no option but to protest as its grievances were not being heard by the authorities. “People say that the PTI does politics of chaos, unrest and protests; however, it would not have resorted to these if it had been heard by the authorities.” He claimed Imran had been jailed unlawfully. “The PTI founder is in solitary confinement and denied his rights. No one is allowed to meet him — not me, his family, lawyers or personal physicians.” After exhausting all constitutional and legal means, he said, the PTI had no other option but to protest. “We are holding a peaceful protest. The Constitution allows us to do so, so the authorities will have to hear us.” He reiterated that the PTI wanted justice for its founder and wanted his cases to be heard on merit, with access to his personal doctors and quality medical treatment. He further claimed that the KP police had faced interference from the federal government and other institutions. The chief minister also distanced the provincial government from cases registered against journalists in KP, saying it would never allow such actions. On a proposal to create new provinces in Pakistan, CM Afridi said it was the PTI founder’s vision to establish new administrative units across the country. “But the question is: who will create them? Only a government with a mandate can do so,” he said, adding, “We support the call for creating new administrative units, but only through a government brought to power by the people.” Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023 — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in the £190m case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case . An accountability court in Islamabad had sentenced Imran and Bushra to 14 and seven years in prison, respectively, on Jan 17, 2025, in the case. Subsequently, both had challenged their convictions before the IHC. The case alleges that the couple obtained billions of rupees and land worth hundreds of kanals from Bahria Town Ltd to legalise Rs50 billion identified and returned to the country by the United Kingdom during the PTI government.

New investigation team initiates formal proceedings into Mir Raza Ali murder. A new investigation team formed by the Sindh IGP on Monday initiated formal proceedings into the murder of business owner Mir Raza Ali, following the findings of a second post-mortem examination. Owner of eatery Wafflix, Ali had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar. The deceased’s family, along with their lawyer, Jibran Nasir, met members of the new investigation team at the DIG Crime office. The team also met investigators from the previous team and obtained records related to the case. DIG Crime and Investigation Amir Farooqi, who heads the new team, told Dawn that the investigators heard the family and their lawyer in detail about the circumstances surrounding Ali’s murder. “The police will keep the family informed of all steps being taken to solve the case,” he said. He said the new team had obtained the investigation records from the previous team to review the entire case file. Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said earlier today that the provincial government had deferred the decision on the formation of a judicial commission to probe the Mir Raza Ali murder case. Lanjar made the announcement on X, saying that Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab had spoken to Ali’s family, who had expressed “confidence in the new police team” constituted to investigate the case and was of the view that it should conduct the probe. “Therefore, the decision of establishing a judicial commission has been deferred for the time being,” the home minister said. While his family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide. A murder charge was eventually added to the first information report after the exhumation and a second postmortem of Ali’s body revealed that he had suffered multiple injuries and was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide. Controversy fueled by ‘miscommunication’ Sindh Inspector General of Police (IGP) Javed Alam Odho said that the investigation into the murder should be conducted in a better manner, expressing hope that the new investigation team would consider all available evidence. Speaking to the media in Sukkur, he said the government, public and police were all concerned about the case and stressed the need to examine it “with an open mind and open heart”. He said action had been taken against officers found guilty of misconduct and negligence during the investigation. IG Odho said the controversy surrounding Ali’s murder had been fuelled by “miscommunication”. “I have strictly instructed the entire investigation team to keep communication open and transparent this time, whether with the deceased’s family or the media,” he said. On Sunday, PPP leader Faryal Talpur recommended a judicial commission to probe the case, saying it should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light. A few hours after Talpur’s statement, Lanjar and Wahab had reached Ali’s residence, met with his father, Mir Hussain Ali, and assured the family that they would be provided complete justice. Talking to the media after the meeting, Lanjar had said a decision had been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry, under the supervision of a Sindh High Court judge, into the murder case. However, Jibran Nasir, the family’s lawyer, posted on X that they had not requested or consented to any judicial commission. “Nor do we believe it’s required at this stage. A new investigation team has been formed, which the family will meet tomorrow. The Sindh government should not try to create hurdles/confusion in the name of ‘facilitation,’“ he said. He had earlier also objected to the initially constituted police team probing the case and demanded that it be replaced. Speaking to the media on Saturday after the results of the second autopsy came out, he had said that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team. Subsequently, the Sindh inspector general of police’s office notified on Sunday the reconstitution of the investigating team probing the case. The order to this effect said the new investigation team was formed in light of Ali’s second postmortem report, which contradicted the one released after his first postmortem. The same day, Karachi police chief Azad Khan also suspended Sharea Faisal Sub-divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar Station House Officer (SHO) Kamran Qureshi with immediate effect for failing to preserve the crime scene and conduct a proper crime-scene investigation after Ali’s body was found. The city police chief also ordered the case be transferred to Zaman Town Police Station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was initially registered. Controversy over autopsy The latest developments in the case follow a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination. Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel last week that the post-mortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. The police surgeon, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself back then, had said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case. Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation. The statement, however, said that exhumation of the body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission. On August 6, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation. The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed. But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts. The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on Saturday. After a second postmortem of the body, Dr Syed told Dawn that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back, which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exited from the front,” she said. She said the body bore “injuries in the right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in the mouth and throat”.

Petrol will continue to be sold at Rs327.62 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs380.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 11. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

3rd phase of AJK elections: PML-N poised for gains in Poonch amid rigging allegations. The PML-N appeared set to gain at least one seat in Poonch division, where four constituencies went to the polls on Monday amid allegations of rigging, violence and disruption, with polling suspended at some places. The biggest upset was the defeat of Muslim Conference president Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan in LA-14 (Dhirkot), a constituency from where he, and before him his uncle and father, had been elected in all nine elections since 1985. His defeat also appeared to underscore the political decline of what was once the largest and longest-ruling party in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), but was reduced to a marginal force following the emergence of the PML-N in 2010. Khan was defeated by Sajid Iqbal Abbasi, who contested his first election on the ticket of the little-known Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party, by a margin of more than 21,000 votes, according to unofficial and unverified results from 213 of the 214 polling stations. Observers attributed Abbasi’s victory largely to his hands-on efforts for the development of the constituency and the welfare of its residents, which, they said, had helped him build a personal support base over the years. PML-N’s Raja Faisal Azad and PPP’s Raja Mubashar Ejaz secured 3,000 and 2,800 votes, respectively. In another closely watched contest in LA-17 (Haveli), a neck-and-neck fight was under way between Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore and PML-N candidate Engr Chaudhry Mohsin Aziz. Initial reports suggested that Aziz had established a sizeable lead, but it later emerged that results from nearly two dozen polling stations were still awaited. Independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed, who had initially been tipped to finish second, was trailing far behind. In LA-15 (Bagh Central), Jamaat-i-Islami’s Brig (retd) Dr Mohammad Khan was initially reported to be heading for victory, but the contest later narrowed to a two-way race between PML-N’s Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas and PPP’s Sardar Ziaul Qamar. Late-night unofficial and unverified results showed Qamar establishing a clear lead of 2,000 votes over Mr Minhas. Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) president and former AJK prime minister Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, who had won the constituency in the 2021 election on a PTI ticket, appeared to be out of the race. In LA-16 (Bagh East), PML-N’s Sardar Mir Akbar was leading PPP’s Sardar Qamaruz Zaman, who is the father of the PPP candidate in LA-15 and has served as an AJK minister in several PPP governments. Akbar had secured 14,900 votes, while Mr Qamar had polled 10,960. Results from 14 polling stations were awaited. Elections are being held across AJK in phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Citing law and order concerns, the Election Commission had decided to postpone polling in Bagh and Sudhnoti districts that was originally set for today. Polling began at 8am and continued until 5pm in four Poonch constituencies. The PPP, which has accused the PML-N of rigging in the previous phases, continued to make similar allegations on Monday as well. In response, PML-N leaders said the PPP had no evidence for its claims, and reiterated their confidence to form the government in AJK based on the seats it has already secured so far. The PML-N has so far bagged 24 seats — nine from Mirpur polls held on July 27 and 15 in the second phase comprising Muzaffarabad Division and the 12 refugee seats. On the other hand, the PPP has only won 10 constituencies so far. The third phase of the AJK elections was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division. The division comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district. However, last week the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli due to concerns over the law and order situation. The AJK election commissioner has hinted that polling on the remaining seven constituencies could be held by Aug 20 or 21. Government officials had anticipated clashes in some areas today, while the Election Commission had classified most of the 803 polling stations in the four constituencies as either sensitive or highly sensitive. “Apart from the regular police of both districts, we have dispatched an additional 10,300 troops to maintain law and order and provide a fear-free atmosphere to voters,” Election Commission Secretary Raja Mohammad Shakeel told Dawn earlier Malpractice, rigging allegations Polling in previous phases of the elections was marred by allegations of rigging , scuffles and violence, with the PPP and the PML-N — the main contenders in AJK but allies in the Centre — engaging in a war of words. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging and electoral malpractices in the previous phases. It continued to allege rigging in Haveli and Bagh as well. In a series of posts on X, the PPP shared complaints it said it had filed to the Election Commission. In one of the complaints, the PPP alleged that roads leading to the Banni Marasira area had been blocked, where PML-N supporters were illegally stamping ballot papers at 12 polling stations in the LA-15 constituency. “The commission is requested to consider the two acts together rather than separately, because the second is made possible by the first,” the party said, adding that officials, voters, polling agents and party workers were unable to reach the polling stations “to see what is being done inside”. The party also claimed delays in polling at LA-15’s polling station no.87 in Thub. It also alleged that polling at stations no.143 and 144 in Hatala Pader did not commence on time due to the non-arrival of polling staff. The PPP also alleged that its polling agent was “forcibly removed” from LA-15’s station no.158 in Makhdoom Kot. Similarly, PPP’s agents had also been removed from polling stations no.8-14 in Bani Maldhara and PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers at those stations, the party alleged. At around 12:45, the party claimed on X that workers of Jamaat-i-Islami had gathered to “capture” 26 polling stations in the constituency — nos.31-38, nos.70-79 and nos.180-186. It said the police had initially arrived but then withdrew. “The stations are, therefore, unguarded at this moment, with an organised body assembled against them.” It urged the Election Commission to determine on whose orders police had withdrawn and direct the law enforcers to return to the station. The PPP also posted a blurry video, which it said was of PML-N workers “attacking” the polling station set up at the Boys Middle School in LA-15 Central Bagh. Regarding LA-16, the party claimed that its polling agents were not being allowed inside stations no.119 and 120 while PML-N supporters were stamping ballot papers inside the stations in the agents’ absence. The PPP further alleged delays in polling at stations no.61 and 141 of the constituency. It made similar allegations regarding polling stations no.109 and 110 in LA-16 Bagh-III Sharqi. Moreover, the party accused “armed individuals associated with the PML-N” of opening fire at polling station no.179, Kot Chinalla in the constituency and disrupting the election process. “The polling agents of the PPP have been removed from the station. It is further alleged that ballot papers are being stamped lawfully,” the PPP added. In LA-17, the party alleged that its agents had been “forced out” from the polling station in Mullah Basti, Kahuta City by PML-N workers. PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman expressed reservations after reports of rigging and malpractices emerged, saying that preventing polling agents from entering polling stations in LA-16 raised “serious questions” about the transparency of the election process. In a statement, she demanded that an explanation be sought from the presiding officers of stations nos.119 and 120 on the matter. The senator also called for the Election Commission to take notice of the reports of PPP’s polling agent being removed from station no.158 in LA-15. Rehman further demanded alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortage of polling staff and material, calling on the authorities to ensure that free and transparent elections were held at all polling stations without any disruption. PPP Secretary General Nayyar Bokhari also accused the PML-N of continuing rigging in the third phase of the elections. He highlighted that his party was regularly informing the Election Commission about the alleged rigging via phone. But, “the chief election commissioner and the election commission secretary’s reply to all of our complaints has been that nothing has happened and everything is good,” he claimed. When Dawn approached the Election Commission regarding Bokhari’s claim, Secretary Raja Muhammad Shakeel said any complaint that he or the chief election commissioner received was being attended and responded to, and the Quick Response Force (QRF) was also moved over it. ‘AJK’s people have supported PML-N’ Responding to PPP’s allegations, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said the rival party had not provided any proof for its claims. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad flanked by Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, Sanaullah denied that a comparatively high turnout could be considered proof of rigging. The PML-N leader explained that a strong family and tribe system in AJK prompted people to show up for their relatives. “Our opposing candidate Chaudhry Yasin was complaining yesterday that in his opposing candidate’s union council (UC), 80pc votes were cast, whereas in his own UC, 96pc votes were cast,” Sanaullah claimed. Sanaullah asserted that balloting had gone fairly smoothly in Bagh and Haveli today. He, however, detailed a few reported incidents. In Haveli, people tried to snatch documents from the polling agents in one station, but the Quick Response Force (QRF) promptly responded and resolved the situation without incident, according to Sanaullah. In Bagh, some people, whom Sanaullah claimed were PPP workers, tried to halt polling at three stations. QRF responded there as well and resumed polling, the minister added. Meanwhile, Muqam urged PPP to review the number of people attending their rallies instead of accusing others of rigging, insisting that PPP lacked support from the people of AJK. “AJK’s people have supported PML-N,” Muqam asserted. Disputing PPP’s recent stance that it was against phased elections, Muqam said the party had mentioned no reservations when the election schedule was first announced . Sanaullah also backed Muqam, saying that PPP had not raised concerns when the Election Commission had originally sought consent from all parties for phased elections. He further claimed that upon PPP’s insistence, the electoral watchdog had scheduled voting on the 12 refugee seats in the second phase of the elections. Sanaullah contended that PPP did not want election results from the refugee seats in the rest of Pakistan to impact its numbers in AJK polls since PPP had not even canvassed in those places. Speaking about the recent unrest in the region, Sanaullah expressed hope that the protests would end once the third phase of elections concludes, as protesters had “only aimed to stop elections”. The new AJK government, which he said PML-N would form with a two-thirds majority, will respond to the protesters’ “valid demands”, the PML-N leader added. However, he also warned that those who “took up arms and instigated the people of AJK, while acting on the directions of the enemy… will have to face the law and answer for their crimes”. In response to a reporter’s question about PPP’s claim that PML-N only had numbered days of rule in the Centre, Sanaullah expressed hope that after the AJK elections, PPP would “open-heartedly” congratulate PML-N. Meanwhile, PML-N’s AJK chapter secretary general Tariq Farooq — who also emerged as the winner in LA-7 recently — said allegations of “rigging, violence, coercion, or fake voting” emerging from the constituency of Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore were a “serious question of constitutional governance”. “This is no longer merely an electoral dispute. It becomes a serious question of constitutional governance, democratic values, and the sanctity of the people’s vote,” Farooq wrote on X. “I find it difficult to believe that the prime minister of Azad Jammu & Kashmir could consider himself above the Constitution, the law, and basic ethical obligations merely to secure his own election,” he said, without providing further details. The PML-N candidate asserted that “public mandate must be secured through a free, fair and transparent election, not through power, influence or state authority”. Rathore, two ex-AJK PMs face crucial electoral test In Monday’s polls, AJK PM Rathore, who is from the PPP, and two of his predecessors — Sardar Tanveer Ilyas and Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan — face a battle for political survival as voters head to the polls. Around 238,664 men and 221,707 women are eligible to cast their ballots at 803 polling stations comprising 1,254 polling booths. A total of 82 candidates are in the fray, with LA-14 (Dhirkot) attracting the highest number of candidates at 30 and LA-17 (Haveli) the lowest at nine. In LA-17, Rathore is facing PML-N candidate Mohsin Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed, a member of the AJK Council. Rathore and Saeed had been political allies and, under an agreement, had agreed to contest the seat alternately. However, after becoming prime minister, Rathore asked Saeed to step aside in his favour, a request he did not accept, turning the former allies into rivals. Aziz, whose father Chaudhry Mohammad Aziz had won the seat at least three times, draws support from the sizeable Gujjar community. His recent large election rally in Forward Kahuta reportedly surprised his rivals and underscored the strength of his campaign. Saeed, meanwhile, is believed to enjoy the backing of a sizeable section of the Kashmiri community, as well as an alliance of several smaller clans. Rathore, however, remains confident of retaining the seat, citing the performance of his government during his relatively brief tenure as prime minister. The constituency has also witnessed allegations of electoral irregularities on social media, with reports claiming that two presiding officers had been caught manipulating results in favour of Rathore. Shakeel dismissed the allegations but at the same time confirmed that complaints had been received against the two officials and that they had subsequently been relieved of election duties. In LA-15 (Wasti Bagh), ex-PM Ilyas is facing PML-N candidate and former minister Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas, PPP nominee and sitting minister Sardar Ziaul Qamar, and Jamaat-i-Islami candidate retired Brig Dr Mohammad Khan, a respected educationist. Ilyas, who secured a little over 3,300 votes from Upper Neelum in the second phase of the elections, had initially announced a boycott of the third phase. He subsequently reversed the decision and resumed campaigning, claiming that his victory would enable the constituency to “secure either the presidency or prime ministership.” Ilyas and Qamar belong to the same Madiyal tribe, while Brig Khan belongs to the Narma clan and enjoys the support of former JI chief Abdul Rashid Turabi and former adviser Raja Yasin Khan. Minhas has the advantage of belonging to the PML-N, which is poised to form the next government after emerging as the largest party in the elections held so far. His campaign has also stressed the argument that voters should elect a candidate from the party that is set to occupy the government benches rather than send their representative to the opposition. In LA-16 (Sharqi Bagh), former ministers Sardar Mir Akbar and Sardar Qamar Zaman are the principal contenders, representing the PML-N and PPP, respectively. The fourth contest, LA-14 (Dhirkot), has drawn particular attention because of the challenge faced by Sardar Attique, head of the once-dominant Muslim Conference (MC). Attique is reportedly facing a strong challenge from Sajid Iqbal Abbasi of the relatively new Awam Dast-o-Bazu Party. A contractor and philanthropist, Abbasi is said to have spent millions of rupees from his own resources on public welfare projects in the constituency, helping him build a sizeable personal following. Attique, who has represented the constituency successively since 2006, when he first became prime minister, faces an additional challenge in that Abbasi also belongs to the same tribe. Among nearly two dozen other candidates are PML-N’s nominee Raja Faisal Azad and PPP candidate Raja Mubashar Ejaz. While the main contest is seen as being between Attique and Abbasi, the PML-N and PPP nominees are expected to vie for the second runner-up position. Additional reporting by Tariq Naqash

DawnMedia to host ‘Act for Nutrition’. KARACHI: As Pakistan faces one of the gravest development challenges of our time, DawnMedia is set to host a landmark national conference on malnutrition and stunting. ‘Act for Nutrition’ will be held on Sept 2 and 3 at the Serena Hotel, Islamabad, to shed light on “the emergency we can no longer ignore”, DawnMedia said in a statement. According to the statement, about 40 per cent of children in Pakistan under the age of five are stunted, while the country has one of the highest child malnutrition numbers in the world. “Maternal malnutrition, widespread micronutrient deficiencies, food insecurity, poor infant feeding practices, rapid population growth and persistent poverty continue to reinforce a cycle of deprivation that spans generations,” the statement said. According to recent estimates, Pakistan loses nearly $17 billion annually due to the economic consequences of malnutrition and undernutrition. Recognising nutrition as fundamentally an economic, governance and developmental challenge, and not solely as a health issue, “Act for Nutrition seeks to elevate malnutrition from a fragmented public health concern to a national development priority”. The conference will bring together policymakers, development partners, healthcare professionals, economists, academics, civil society organisations, humanitarian agencies, and the private sector for two days of evidence-based dialogue. Speakers will examine the country’s nutrition landscape through interconnected lenses of poverty, health, education, climate resilience, governance, and human rights. The principal partners of the conference are the Sindh health ministry, the government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and English Biscuit Manufacturers. The knowledge partners include Globesight, International Research Force, and the Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health Research Network. The organisations bring together expertise to strengthen the dialogue around nutrition and child development in the country. “Act for Nutrition marks the beginning of a long-term natio­nal movement — one that recognises investing in maternal and child nutrition as among the most powerful investments Pak­i­stan can make in its future prosperity, resilience, and human capital,” the statement said. Cabinet okays housing policy, cybersecurity framework. PM Shehbaz Sharif chairs a meeting of the federal cabinet.—Online ISLAMABAD: The federal cabinet on Monday approved the National Housing Policy 2026 along with an action plan for its implementation, directing that housing projects comply fully with zoning laws and that vertical construction be prioritised to make more efficient use of land. The meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad. The cabinet was told that the policy had been prepared by a working group made up of national and international experts, and that federal ministries, provincial governments and development partners had been consulted during the drafting process. Its core objective, members were informed, is the provision of sustainable, safe and quality housing for all citizens. Alongside the zoning and vertical-housing directives, the cabinet instructed that energy-efficiency codes be made an integral part of the National Housing Policy, so that new construction conforms to energy-efficient and environmentally friendly requirements. Housing projects must comply fully with zoning laws and prioritise vertical construction, cabinet rules Members were also briefed on progress under the prime minister’s Apna Ghar scheme. The cabinet was informed that various banks had approved loans worth Rs220 billion for applicants seeking to build or purchase homes, and that more than Rs32 billion had already been disbursed to successful applicants. In a separate decision, the cabinet approved the withdrawal of the notice terminating the 1981 bilateral investment treaty between Pakistan and Sweden. The approval came on a summary submitted to the meeting by the Board of Investment. The Ministry of Information Technology placed before the cabinet the draft Pakistan Information Security Framework 2026, known as PISF 2026. The cabinet was told that the framework had been prepared under the CERT Rules 2023, and that it seeks to establish a comprehensive and unified system of baseline information-security standards while ensuring central oversight. Approving the framework, the cabinet described it as an important guiding document for cybersecurity and directed that its effective implementation be ens­ured within the prescribed timeframe. The cabinet further ratified a decision taken at the meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Energy held on July 28. Under that decision, proposed amendments to the Pakistan Oil Refining Policy 2023 were endorsed, providing for the upgrading of oil refineries so that the country’s energy requirements can be met more effectively. Decisions taken at two meetings of the Economic Coordination Committee, held on July 27 and August 4, were also ratified, as were decisions taken at the meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Legislative Cases held on July 24. Retrospective tax penalties are ‘unlawful’: Supreme Court. • Says sanctions under ITO 2001 cannot apply to assessments governed by repealed law • Settles conflict between two previous rulings ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Monday ruled that penalties imposed under the Income Tax Ordinance (ITO) 2001 for assessments completed before June 30, 2002 were illegal and legally unsustainable, emphasising that such penalties could not be applied retrospectively. A five-judge SC larger bench, headed by Justice Shahid Waheed, also resolved a conflict between two decisions of three-member benches — the 2009 Eli Lilly Pakistan (Pvt) Ltd case and the 2016 Islamic Investment Bank Ltd case. The question before the SC was whether penalties under Sections 182, 184 and 186 of the ITO 2001 were lawful in view of the provisions of Section 239(3) of the ordinance. Authored by Justice Aqeel Ahmed Abbasi, the 17-page judgement explained that in the Eli Lilly Pakistan case, the court had held that assessments completed under the repealed ITO 1979 must be governed strictly by the old law, while assessments made after its repeal were to be governed by the ITO 2001. However, in the Islamic Investment Bank case, the court had taken a contrary view, departing from the strict prospective approach and declaring that the right of the state to calculate and collect the correct tax liability vests at the end of each accounting year. The judgment held that the conclusion drawn by the subsequent bench of co-equal strength in the Islamic Investment Bank case was erroneous in law, whereas the decision of the earlier co-equal bench in the Eli Lilly case, treating the amendments as substantive in nature and prospective in application, reflected the correct legal position. The controversy revolves around Khadim Hussain, the respondent and an existing taxpayer falling under the jurisdiction of the director general of Regional Tax Office, Rawalpindi. The case arose when the petitioner, commissioner inland revenue (legal), RTO Rawalpindi, initiated tax proceedings against the respondent after receiving information that he had purchased a piece of property on Sept 7, 1999, without filing a corresponding tax return. Following his non-compliance with notices issued under Sections 61 and 62, a notice under Section 13(1) (aa) was served on June 28, 2007, requiring the respondent to explain the source of investment for the property. Due to the respondent’s continuous non-appearance and failure to submit documentary evidence, an ex-parte assessment was framed under Section 63 of the repealed ITO 1979, creating a tax addition of Rs300,000 for the assessment years 2000-01 to 2002-3, along with the imposition of a penalty under Section 184 of the ITO, read with Section 111 of the repealed ordinance. Subsequent compliance and reminder notices issued under Section 190 also went unheeded. Aggrieved by the assessment and pena-lty orders, the respondent filed an appeal before the commissioner of income tax (appeals), which upheld the income addition but deleted the penalties on Jan 31, 2008. The tax department preferred a second appeal before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, challenging the deletion of the penalties. The appeal was subsequently dismissed on the ground that the penalties were legally unsustainable under Section 239. The department then approached the Rawalpindi bench of Lahore High Court by filing a reference, which was ultimately dismissed on Oct 27, 2014. Subsequently, the tax department approached the Supreme Court, seeking leave to appeal against the LHC order. Justice Abbasi explained that in the absence of clear legislative language expressly giving retrospective effect to the provisions of the ITO 2001, they could not be invoked in respect of assessments governed by the repealed ITO 1979. Any contrary interpretation, he observed, would undermine the settled principle that a taxpayer’s substantive rights and liabilities crystallise under the law applicable to the relevant assessment year and cannot subsequently be aggravated through later legislation. “It is a well-settled legal position that in a taxing statute, if an amendment is introduced which is penal in nature or increases the tax liability of a taxpayer, it applies prospectively for the tax year in which such amendment has been introduced and cannot be given retrospective effect, unless such retrospective effect is given through the amending law itself in express language,” the judgement explained. The Supreme Court consequently ruled that the penalties imposed under Sections 182, 184 and 186 of the ITO 2001 were unlawful and legally unsustainable. Accordingly, the question proposed in the instant case relating to the imposition of penalties under these sections was held to be legally not maintainable, and the civil appeal was refused. Goods, oil transporters strike continues. KARACHI: A driver passes between trucks parked at the Shireen Jinnah colony terminal, as a wheel-jam strike called by goods transporters affected the movement of cargo across the country for a third consecutive day. Talks between transporters and the government are expected to continue today.—PPI • Next round of talks with govt today • KCCI offers to mediate between both sides ISLAMABAD/KARACHI: Talks between striking transporters and the government continued until late Monday night with both sides holding firm on their demands as the deadlock persisted, mainly over fuel pricing and taxes. The next round of negotiations will be held today. As oil tankers, edible oil tankers, trailers, goods transport trucks, etc. went off the road on Friday night ahead of the scheduled strike from Saturday, the government offered talks with the collective body of the striking transporters. As the first round of talks held on Monday morning remained inconclusive with both sides unwilling to yield any ground, the second round of negotiations commenced later in the afternoon. The transporters have presented three main demands, each related to different ministries. The first demand, to increase the permissible weight for 10-wheeler vehicles to 35 tonnes from the current 27.5 tonnes, as well as reduce toll tax rates, relates to the National Highways Authority (NHA) and the communications ministry. The other demand was that diesel pricing should be revised on a monthly basis, as daily price revisions disturb their business planning. The third demand of the transporters relates to customs duties and income tax. The government side was jointly led by Communi­cations Minister Aleem Khan and Petro­leum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik. It included relevant officers from the FBR, ministries, ports and shipping, federal secretaries, and transport secretaries of the four provinces. Meanwhile, the strikers gathered under the platform of the All Pakistan Goods Transport Ittehad alliance, which includes representatives of various associations. The spokesman for the alliance, Advo­cate Moham­mad Owais Chaudhry, told Dawn that negotiations between the transporters and the government were underway, but no decision had been reached so far. “We have clearly presented our position before the government and will not show any flexibility on it,” he said. He added that the government had to accept the transporters’ demands for the strike to end. Meanwhile, a senior official in the government negotiating team said the daily fuel adjustment had been made due to volatility in international markets and was not a local issue. However, the government was considering lowering toll tax for heavy vehicles, while the axle load could also be amended. KCCI offer In Karachi, businessmen and exporters have warned that continued suspension of cargo movement would hit industrial production, supply chains, exports and the country’s overall economic activities. Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) President Muhammad Rehan Hanif, in a statement issued on Monday, urged the federal as well as all provincial governments to immediately engage representatives of the transport sector at the highest level. He warned that any prolonged disruption in the movement of goods and petroleum products could have a cascading impact on industrial production, availability of raw materials, delivery of finished products, fuel supplies, domestic commerce and export shipments. He asked stakeholders in the transport sector to consider the enormous damage being caused to the country by the strike. He urged them to call off the strike in the larger interest of Pakistan, expressing hope that the government would engage with them and that their legitimate demands could be discussed and resolved through negotiations. “The KCCI is ready to play its role as a mediator,” Mr Hanif said. Pakistan Textile Council (PTC) Chairman Fawad Anwar, in a letter to the prime minister, said the strike from Saturday could severely affect Pakistan’s textile and apparel supply chains and export shipments. He highlighted that Pakistan’s textile and apparel industry relies heavily on uninterrupted transportation to move imported and locally sourced raw materials to manufacturing units and to ensure finished export consignments reach ports on time. The PTC chairman acknowledged that the transporters’ demands involved matters requiring coordination among different levels and departments of the government. However, he cautioned that the economic cost of the continuing deadlock would increase with every passing day. He requested PM Shehbaz Sharif to bring the relevant government authorities and representatives of the transport sector together to secure an early resolution of the strike. Remittances rise 13pc to $3.6bn in July. KARACHI: Remitta­nces sent by overseas Pakistanis in the first month of the current fiscal year met the government’s expectations, with significant growth compared with the preceding month. The latest data issued by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Monday showed that inflows were 13 per cent higher in July than in the same month of the previous fiscal year. The country received a total of $3.6 billion in July, compared with $3.2bn in the same month last year. Month-on-month, the growth was 4.5pc. The inflows are encouraging for the government, which has set an ambitious $44bn remittance target for FY27, up from $41.5bn in FY26. Inflows from Middle East stay robust amid ongoing war Despite more than five months of the war in the Middle East, remittances did not decline; instead, they increased compared with the preceding year. There were some reports of Pakistanis leaving the UAE, but remittances from the Emirates remained intact and, in fact, increased despite the war in FY26. Currency experts said that thousands of Pakistanis have migrated to the Middle East for jobs despite the war; most of them have gone to Saudi Arabia. They said the government is likely to meet the FY27 target. Remittances have not only left export proceeds far behind but have also helped the SBP to improve its foreign exchange reserves. The central bank is a regular buyer of US dollars in the interbank market, but SBP reserves are still largely composed of deposits placed by Saudi Arabia and China, which together account for more than 50pc. Despite the huge inflow of remittances in FY26, the current account remained negative, with the trade deficit of over $39bn consuming most of them. The current year also began with a $3.5bn trade deficit, which alarmed the economy’s stakeholders, who feel the cheaper dollar is leading to higher imports and an unmanageable deficit. Pakistan has failed to increase exports to China despite Beijing now being Islamabad’s largest trading partner, and the trade balance remains largely in China’s favour. Moreover, under-invoicing and smuggling from China are also very high, as the Pakistani market is flooded with Chinese products nationwide. The major corridors of workers’ remittances in July were Saudi Arabia ($913.9m), the UAE ($737.3m), the UK ($555.5m), the US ($317.2m), and EU countries ($452m). Published in Dawn, August 11th, 2026

Major earthquake claims 111 lives in Colombia. PEREIRA: At least 111 people were killed after a powerful earthquake str­uck western Colombia ear­ly on Monday, knocking down buildings across several cities and injuring 87 others, with still more residents trapped in the rubble. The 7.4-magnitude qua­ke, with its epicenter in the coastal Choco region at a depth of 100km, struck at 7:34am, triggering a frantic search for survivors in several cities and thrusting the new administration into its first major crisis as Colombia declared a state of emergency. “The national government is maintaining all its capacities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid to every area that needs it,” President Abelardo de la Espriella stated from Bogota. SBP warns of price spirals. KARACHI: Evolving geopolitical developments in the Middle East could push up global energy and other commodity prices beyond assumed levels, thereby affecting the macroeconomic outlook, warned the State Bank’s biannual Monetary Policy Report (MRR), issued on Monday. Aligning with the State Bank’s commitment to transparency in monetary policy decisions and the MPC’s reaction function, the SBP issued its biannual MPR. The report analyses macroeconomic developments and the outlook that influenced monetary policy since the January MPC meeting. The report highlighted climate-related risks, specifically the evolving El Nino conditions and floods, which could adversely affect the economy. Moreover, delays in implementation of structural reforms could further weaken exports, slow productivity gains, and reduce the economy’s capacity to sustain higher growth without generating inflationary and external account pressures, it added. Mideast conflict may lift energy, commodity prices The macroeconomic conditions and outlook during the review period have been significantly influenced by evolving geopolitical developments, the report said. The outbreak of the Middle East conflict in late February led to sharp increases in global energy prices and freight and insurance costs, as well as supply chain disruptions, it said. Despite this significant shock, the macroeconomic outcomes in FY26 turned out broadly in line with the projection ranges announced after the January Monetary Policy Committee meeting, said the SBP. The report highlighted that the SBP’s prudent monetary policy tightening is helping contain second-round effects of the energy price shock, while keeping inflation expectations of stakeholders anchored. Meanwhile, the government ensured fiscal discipline by raising domestic fuel prices in a timely manner and by introducing targeted subsidies and austerity measures to conserve energy, the report added. These measures helped moderate aggregate demand and kept demand-side pressures muted. The report said that inflation is expected to ease and stabilise near the upper bound of the target range towards the end of FY27. Economic growth is expected to pick up and remain in the range of 3.5-4.5pc. In the external account, the current account deficit is projected to remain within 0-1pc of GDP. This will support continued FX purchases by the SBP and help achieve the FX reserves target of $20.20bn by December 2026. SBP’s FX reserves are projected to rise further by end-FY27, said the report. The report also discusses multiple risks to the macroeconomic outlook. They relate to an update on the monetary policy transmission mechanism; the central bank’s reaction function when faced with supply-side-driven inflation; the use of different measures of inflation globally and within the SBP; the growing size of open market operations and its implications for monetary policy; and the use of various sentiment surveys to gauge stakeholders’ expectations about different aspects of the economy.
