House gets hands on record P7.2-trillion 2027 budget; eyes continued transparency. The House of Representatives under Speaker Faustino "Bojie" Dy III is looking to repeat the conduct of a transformative and transparent budget process this year, even as the flood control projects corruption scandal remains more than a memory to most Filipinos. This, after the House fomally received the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP) worth P7.2 trillion from Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Acting Secretary Kim Robert de Leon in a simple turnover ceremony on Tuesday, Aug. 11. The biggest in history, the 2027 NEP serves as the basis for the General Appropriations Bill (GAB), or the House's legislated budget measure, for next year. The GAB is expected to be filed by the House leadership following the initial hearings of the Committee on Appropriations on the NEP. De Leon said the 2027 spending plan is 6 percent higher that the current P6.793 trillion General Appropriations Act (GAA), or the enacted national budget. Nueva Ecija 1st district Rep. Mikaela Angela "Mika" Suansing currently chairs the appropriations panel. She was also present Tuesday along with Majority Leader Ilocos Norte 1st district Rep. Sandro Marcos and Minority Leader 4Ps Party-list Rep. Marcelino "Nonoy" Libanan, and Senior Deputy Speaker South Cotabato 2nd district Rep. Ferdinand Hernandez. "Masusi nating susuriin ang bawat bahagi ng panukala (We will carefully study every part of the proposal)," Speaker Dy said in his speech before receiving the NEP from the DBM chief. The 2027 budget process will be the first to be fully carried out under the watchful eye of Dy. The Isabela 6th district representative took over as Speaker on Sept. 17, 2025 --roughly a month into the committee-level hearings of the 2026 NEP. Sweeping reforms and pro-transparency measures were implemented during last year's budget process as it directly preceeded President Marcos' fourth State of the Nation Address (SONA), wherein he exposed the anomaly on "ghost" and substandard flood control projects. These innovations include the formation of the Budget Amendments and Review Subcommittee (BARSc) and the livestreaming of the budget bicameral committee deliberations. Rep. Marcos said at the start of the second regular session late last month that these innovations would continue for the 2027 budget process. The passage of the GAB in the House and eventually, the Senate is considered the most important act of Congress every year. Dy vowed to "keep the process open and transparent" this year. "Ang budget ay pera ng taumbayan. May karapatan silang malaman kung saan ito mapupunta. Sisikapin po natin na maging mas bukas pa ang pagbubuo ng ating national budget," he said. (The budget is the people’s money. They have the right to know where it will go. We will strive to make the crafting of our national budget even more open.) SONA-guided budget According to the Speaker, President Marcos emphasized in his July 27 SONA that every peso saved from waste, misuse, and corruption could be allocated to classrooms, hospitals, food, jobs, agriculture, and other services directly needed by Filipinos. "Hindi sapat na sabihin kung magkano ang ginagastos. Dapat maipakita kung ano ang nagagawa ng bawat piso. Ang bawat piso ay dapat may katumbas na ainhawa para sa bawat Pilipino," Dy said. (It is not enough to say how much is being spent. It must be shown what each peso accomplishes. Every peso must translate into relief for every Filipino.) "lyan ang ating pananagutan: tiyaking ang pondo ay may malinaw na layunin, ang mga programa ay may tunay na pakinabang, at ang bawat desisyon ay may positibong epekto sa buhay ng mga Pilipino," the House leader further said. (That is our responsibility: to ensure that funds have clear purpose, programs bring real benefits, and every decision has a positive impact on the lives of Filipinos.) "Dala natin ang hamon ng Pangulo sa pagtatapos ng kanyang SONA: tapusin ang mga nasimulan at tuparin ang ating mga pangako sa sambayanan," he underscored. (We carry the President’s challenge at the close of his SONA: to finish what has been started and fulfill our promises to the nation.)

Wilcon Depot continues expansion as earnings inch higher. Home improvement and construction supply retailer Wilcon Depot Inc. reported that its net income inched up 3.5 percent to ₱1.2 billion in the first half of 2026 as net sales grew 10.9 percent to ₱18.98 billion. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, Aug. 11, the firm said revenue growth was traced mainly to comparable sales growth, which rose 6.6 percent year-on-year, while all regions, including project sales, recorded positive comparable sales growth rates during the half. On a per-format basis, depots, accounting for 96.3 percent of total net sales, grew by 10.9 percent year-on-year to ₱18.27 billion, with same-store sales driving the increase with 6.6-percent growth over the same period last year. Net sales from smaller Do It Wilcon formats (DIWs) contributed 3.2 percent of total net sales and grew by 12.4 percent to ₱607 million for the first half. The increase was driven almost equally by same-store sales growth of 6.1 percent and sales from new stores. Project sales contributed the remaining 0.5 percent, totaling ₱96 million for the period. Gross profit amounted to ₱7.08 billion, increasing by seven percent due mainly to higher sales, partly offset by the contraction in the gross profit margin rate to 37.3 percent due to sales mix. Lower-margin non-exclusive product sales growth outperformed the sales growth of the exclusive and in-house brands, resulting in the decrease in the contribution of the latter to total net sales to 50.5 percent from 52.3 percent during the same period last year. “Our second-quarter results showed solid demand, with total sales up 12.7 percent and same-store sales rising 8.4 percent,” said Wilcon President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Lorraine Belo-Cincochan. She noted, “Every region delivered positive same-store sales growth. The mix shifted toward lower-margin non-exclusive products, which brought down our blended gross profit margin. Operating expenses (opex) also increased in the quarter, driven largely by factors outside our control, though the cost measures we have in place are already helping to ease the impact.” “We are encouraged by the gains in customer count and sales volume. These show we are reaching more customers and give us room to improve the product mix and manage costs in the second half,” Belo-Cincochan added. Wilcon opened five new stores in the first half, and while these new stores contributed substantially to the opex increase, below-one-year stores for the first half still generated positive net income. “We are targeting to open three more stores for the rest of the year. We have so far spent ₱1.2 billion in capital expenditures (capex) with the bulk spent on construction of new stores and warehouses,” Belo-Cincochan said. Net sales in the second quarter of 2026 amounted to ₱9.81 billion, up 12.7 percent year-on-year, driven mainly by comparable sales growth of 8.4 percent. Net income for the quarter totaled ₱641 million, up 2.4 percent year-on-year. Except for project sales, all regions delivered positive same-store sales. During the period, two new small-format DIW branches were opened in Luzon. - James A. Loyola

Park Geon-roung, best known as the 'Baby Shark' boy, makes Kpop debut. The little boy who gained worldwide fame for his appearance in the “Baby Shark" video will make his K-pop debut on Aug. 20. According to The Pinkfong Company, Park Geon-roung is set to release his first digital single titled "WAVE," a Korean-language track with lyrics he co-wrote himself, featuring Joohoney of K-pop group Monsta X. Park reemerged just last year to celebrate "Baby Shark's" 10th year anniversary. "I've always been grateful that people still remember a video I appeared in as a kid," he said in a statement. "Ten years ago I was dancing next to Baby Shark. Now, I wanted to share my own voice and a story I wrote myself. I'm happy to start something new with the people who've remembered me all this time, and I want to keep showing how I grow from here." "Baby Shark Boy grew up alongside Baby Shark and built a special connection with fans around the world. This isn't just about bringing back the boy from the video. It's about him telling his own story, and we want to carry that new beginning forward authentically," a company representative said.

Hontiveros pushes for Senate inquiry into ‘provisional understanding’ on WPS resupply missions. Senator Risa Hontiveros is now pushing for a Senate inquiry into the supposed “provisional understanding” between the Philippine government and China regarding resupply missions to Ayungin Shoal. Hontiveros, in filing Senate Resolution No. 589, said there is a need for the public to know about the existence of such an agreement between the two governments in light of China’s continued aggression in the area. “The only question is, is this agreement working? Because if it is to prevent trouble and protect our soldiers, why do they continue to be harmed while they are just doing their job?” Hontiveros said. “The Senate needs to see exactly what was agreed upon, and whether the Philippines is actually benefitting from it,” the senator pointed out. In her resolution, Hontiveros cited the string of incidents that casts doubt on the effectivity of the deal, including a June 2024 confrontation that cost a Filipino sailor his thumb, a March 2026 incident in which a fire-control radar was directed at Philippine Navy frigate BRP Miguel Malvar, and a July 2026 attack at Ayungin itself in which a Philippine Navy personnel was struck with a wooden baton and had to be medically evacuated. The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) claimed that the deal is meant to avoid miscalculation during Philippine missions to the BRP Sierra Madre, and does not require the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to seek China’s permission or allow Chinese boarding of Philippine vessels. But Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro has said no such deal exists. “The DFA cannot claim there is an agreement while the DND says there isn’t. These are the agencies responsible for our foreign relations and national defense. It needs to be clear to both of them—and especially to our soldiers on the ground—what our policy actually is,” she said. “This deal is supposed to calm our waters. Instead, our soldiers keep coming home injured. Either the agreement isn’t working, or it was never designed to protect us in the first place,” she added. “I am not saying that information truly sensitive to national security needs to be disclosed. But confidentiality cannot be used to hide from the public an agreement that affects our territory, our rights, and the lives of those we send there,” Hontiveros said. In filing the resolution, Hontiveros also invoked the Constitution’s guarantee of full public disclosure of government transactions involving public interest, particularly one affecting jurisdiction over the country’s maritime zones, sovereign rights, and the safety of Filipino personnel. “The West Philippine Sea issue is not something we can afford to negotiate in the dark. We do not need to escalate the conflict. But we need to be clear and firm,” Hontiveros said. “Let us find out what has been agreed upon, improve coordination among our agencies, and ensure that no Filipino soldier is sent on a mission without a clear plan for their protection. We should not be groping in the dark within our own waters,” she stressed. “The Filipino people have every right to know about what is being decided in our name, in our waters,” the lawmaker reiterated.

Villafuertes upbeat on National Cybersecurity Agency creation as bill moves forward in plenary. Camarines Sur Reps. Migz Villafuerte (2nd district) and Luigi Villafuerte (5th district) are upbeat over the imminent establishment of the proposed National Cybersecurity Agency (NCSA) under the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT). This, after the recent approval by the House of Representatives on second reading of House Bill (HB) No. 9605 or the “National Cybersecurity and Critical Information Infrastructure Protection (CIIP) Act of 2026". Rep. Migz chairs the House Committee on Information and Communications Technology (ICT), which endorsed the approval of the bill that served as the substitute measure of 26 CIIP or cybersecurity-related bills. In his sponsorship speech on Aug. 3, Rep. Migz said on the plenary floor that cybersecurity was no longer an ICT concern alone, in light of mounting reliance on digital systems in all sectors. He says it has transformed into a national security concern. Hence, he said, the NCSA, as proposed in HB No. 9605, aims to facilitate a whole-of-government approach to handling cybersecurity, beef up response to cyber attacks, establish minimum standards for CIIP, and provide for congressional oversight, judicial review and legal accountability. “The question is no longer whether our country will experience another major cyber attack; the question is whether we are prepared for it when that happens,” said the 2nd district congressman. "And because such a threat has become permanent, our institutional response must also be a permanent one.” The proposed NCSA, he added, would strengthen national coordination, improve incident response, and establish minimum cybersecurity standards for critical information infrastructure. Rep. Luigi noted that the approval of this cybersecurity bill became urgent on the heels of President Marcos’ recent issuance of Executive Order (EO) No. 119, which updated the Government Data Classification Framework of 1964 to accelerate the country’s digital transformation while safeguarding Filipinos against cybersecurity risks. As regards cybersecurity risks, he said that mobile payments service provider GCash, for instance, reported last July having blocked some 6,700 bogus merchant accounts tied to QRPh scams known as "quishing", in which bad actors use phony QR codes to redirect users to fake GCash payment pages or illegitimate accounts to steal cash from the victims. The proposed Cybersecurity Act was among the 48 priority measures that President Marcos identified for urgent action last year with the legislative-Executive Development Advisory Committee (LEDAC). Rep. Migz said, “Ang panukalang batas na ito ang magbibigay ng permanenteng institutional framework upang maprotektahan ang ating mga kritikal na sistema, mapatatag ang ating pambansang katatagan, at mapangalagaan ang tiwala ng ating mga mamamayan sa digital na ekonomiya.” (This proposed law will provide a permanent institutional framework to protect our critical systems, strengthen our national resilience, and safeguard the trust of our citizens in the digital economy.) “Ang cybersecurity ay hindi na lamang usapin ng teknolohiya. Isa na itong usapin ng pambansang seguridad. At kung permanente ang banta, permanente rin dapat ang ating institutional response,” he added. (Cybersecurity is no longer just a matter of technology. It has become a matter of national security. And if the threat is permanent, our institutional response must also be permanent.)

DOLE fines Baldwin, Ateneo P4.9 M for foreign worker permit violation. The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) ordered both basketball coach Thomas Anthony “Tab” Baldwin and the Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) to pay P4.9 million as fine for violating the provisions of the law governing the employment of foreigners. The hefty fine was in connection with the failure of both Baldwin and the ADMU to secure a Certificate of Exemption (COE), since the former started working as the head coach of the school’s men’s basketball team from Feb. 10 last year until his resignation on June 15 this year. Baldwin resigned from his post after the death of Rene Baterbonia and Divine Adili during an off-campus training at a beach resort in Aurora early June this year. The two players drowned during a water activity training. In the decision released on Tuesday, Aug. 11, DOLE explained that the fine reached P4.9 million as it penalized both Baldwin and ADMU P10,000 per day for violation of the provision for a period of 490 days when the former was employed as basketball coach. The same decision also penalized Baldwin and ADMU with P10,000 each— for Baldwin’s failure to obtain Alien Employment Permit (AEP) as a foreign worker, and for ADMU’ failure to do the same as an employer. In issuing the decision, DOLE cited Article 40 of the Labor Code of the Philippines which stated that every foreign national employed in the country is required to have a valid AEP. Baldwin, during a hearing last month, it was found out that Baldwin did not have an AEP and COE as a foreign worker in the country. In the same decision signed by DOLE Secretary Francis Tolentino, it said the case of Baldwin will be referred to the Bureau of Immigration for proper action. “Finally, without prejudice to civil, administrative or criminal complaints pending before other investigative agencies or the courts of law against Mr. Baldwin, this matter is hereby referred to the Bureau of Immigration and Deportation for summary deportation proceedings,” the decision read. The lawyers of both Baldwin and ADMU said they will avail of legal remedies in relation to the decision.

‘Whenever they are ready’: Ateneo makes public appeal to meet Rene Baterbonia’s family. The Ateneo de Manila University (ADMU) has made a public appeal to meet again with the family of late basketball player Rene Baterbonia following a recent podcast interview by his mother, Rovelyn. In a statement issued Monday, Aug. 10, ADMU said it was “heartbreaking” to see the deep pain and loss the Baterbonia family continues to endure following the deaths of Rene and Divine Adili on June 8. The university said it had continued efforts to support the Baterbonia and Adili families and their loved ones, much of which was done quietly out of respect for their privacy and their need to grieve. “We have made every earnest effort to remain in touch with both the Baterbonia and Adili families, while respecting the wishes and circumstances of each family, and continue to do so to this day,” ADMU said. At Rene’s wake in Manila, University President Fr. Bobby Yap personally met with Mrs. Baterbonia to offer his condolences and apologies, pray with her, offer Holy Mass, and assure her that the university was ready to extend whatever help the family needed. Yap visited the wake several times, while other members of the Ateneo community also conveyed the university’s offer of support to the family on different occasions, ADMU said. Following the wake at Ateneo de Davao University, the Baterbonia family brought Rene home to Talacogon, Agusan del Sur, where his wake continued. In the weeks that followed, the family asked the university to give them the space they needed as they prepared for the commemoration of the 40th day of Rene’s death. “We respected their request,” ADMU said. The university said it had since repeated its request to meet with the Baterbonia family but had not yet been given a chance to do so. ADMU said it was now making the appeal publicly in the hope that it could sit down with the family again, listen to them, provide the answers it could, and extend whatever care or support they may need. “We take this opportunity to reach out once again to the Baterbonia family, this time publicly, in the hope that we can finally sit down with them again, listen to them, provide the answers we can, and extend whatever care or support they may need,” the university said. “We remain here for them, whenever they are ready,” it added.

Escudero chides Duterte’s defense team for 'ghosting' prosecution; orders them to submit evidence to impeachment court. Senate Impeachment Court Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero on Tuesday, August 11 reminded the defense lawyers of Vice President Sara Duterte about the need to respond to the prosecution’s messages concerning the stipulation of documents. This, after both sides failed to meet after the impeachment court ordered the defense lawyers to submit to the court its marked evidence from the pre-trial proceedings in order that senator-judges can study the documents. Lorna Kapunan, one of the lawyers of the House prosecution panel, complained that Duterte’s camp snubbed them when they sought a mutually common date and time, saying “eto po ang nangyari: na-Indian po kami (This is what happened: we were ignored).” “The Presiding Officer’s directive to agree on a date—specifically Thursday or Friday of last week—was very clear. That constitutes bad faith, Your Honor, because the Presiding Officer had specified those dates—Thursday or Friday of last week. Yet, the defense claim that the Presiding Officer made nothing of the sort,” Kapunan lamented. Escudero eventually responded: “Hindi ka in-indian, siguro ginhost ka (You weren’t ignored, maybe you were ghosted).” “But having said that…the Chair would like to request the counsels for respondent to kindly furnish the court with a copy of the marked pieces of evidence during pre-trial,” the presiding officer asked the defense panel on Day 14 of the impeachment trial. “So in lieu of meeting, kindly just submit that, Atty. Kristine (Ferrer), so that we can do the comparison ourselves either as a Court or through the individual Senator-Judges,” Escudero further said. Last Wednesday, the Impeachment Court, through Escudero ordered both the prosecution and defense to meet either Thursday or Friday last week so they can agree on the veracity of the documents they possess and will submit as evidence before the tribunal. But Kapunan said they received no reply from the defense, citing that the defense’s stonewalling dragged on until the end of office hours on Thursday last week.

Marcos: Proposed 2027 budget is a ‘prudent, forward-looking investment’. The proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for next year represents a prudent and forward-looking investment aimed at sustaining the country's economic growth, President Marcos said. In his budget message, Marcos said the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), which was submitted to the House of Representatives on Tuesday, Aug. 11, "is more than a strategic investment." "More than a financial plan, it is a strategic investment in the Filipino people and in our country's future," Marcos said in his message. "It translates our priorities into concrete action, ensuring that every public resource contributes to stronger institutions, greater economic opportunities, and a better quality of life for every Filipino," he added. Stressing that the proposed budget underwent a thorough review, Marcos said that from the P11.690 trillion in funding proposals submitted by government agencies, they have carefully determined the programs and projects that will deliver the greatest impact for the people and for national development priorities. "The proposed Php 7.200 trillion FY 2027 National Budget represents a prudent and forward-looking investment that sustains economic growth while remaining firmly consistent with our fiscal consolidation agenda," Marcos said. He said he has directed all agencies to focus on measurable outcomes, align their proposals with the country's development agenda, eliminate unnecessary or inefficient expenditures, and ensure that every peso produces meaningful and lasting value. He assured that these investments remain firmly anchored on the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028 and the Ambisyon Natin 2040. "This budget strengthens our capacity to invest in strategic infrastructure, human capital, food and energy security, and social protection, while reinforcing transparency, accountability, and the efficient use of public resources," he said. According to the Chief Executive, the 2027 NEP seeks to modernize public institutions, improve productivity, strengthen competitiveness, attract greater investments, create quality jobs, and enhance the government's ability to deliver faster, more responsive, and citizen-centered public services. "What distinguishes this expenditure program is its deliberate focus on transformative reforms that will shape the country's long-term development trajectory," he said. "By emphasizing measurable outcomes, institutional reforms, and long-term value creation, the proposed FY 2027 National Budget serves as a catalyst for sustainable and inclusive national development," he added. Marcos emphasized that the proposed budget "recognizes that genuine progress is measured not only through stronger economic indicators, but through the lives we improve-families with greater opportunities, workers with more secure livelihoods, farmers and fisherfolk with stronger support, students with better education, healthier communities, safer neighborhoods, and a government that consistently earns the trust and confidence of its people." The proposed budget, he added, reaffirms the administration's commitment to inclusive growth, sound fiscal management, good governance, and responsible stewardship of public resources. "Together, let us ensure that every peso entrusted to government creates meaningful results today while laying the foundation for a stronger, more resilient, and more prosperous Philippines for generations to come," he said. The House of Representatives formally received the proposed 2027 NEP from Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Acting Secretary Kim Robert de Leon in a simple turnover ceremony on Tuesday.

Death toll due to ‘habagat,’ tropical cyclones increases to 19 as 2.27M affected – OCD. Six more fatalities related to the combined effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) and Tropical Cyclones “Luis” and “Maymay,” bringing the death toll to 19, according to the latest report released by the Office of Civil Defense on Tuesday, Aug. 11. The OCD said the death toll due to a landslide in Barangay Guisad Surong, Baguio City on Sunday rose to nine following the recovery of five more bodies. Separate landslide incidents were previously reported in La Trinidad where two cooks died and in Atok where one person was killed. Meanwhile, one new death due to drowning was listed in Binangonan, Rizal. The OCD earlier recorded two deaths in Rodriguez due to a landslide and one in Antipolo after a delivery rider was struck by a fallen tree. In Batangas, the death toll remained at three: one each in Batangas City, Lipa City, and Santa Teresita town due to drowning, electrocution, and landslide, respectively. The number of injured also increased to 15, with Benguet tallying the most at 12: eight in Baguio, two in La Trinidad, and one each in Kapangan and Atok due to landslides and a vehicular accident. One person was injured in Suyo, Ilocos Sur due to a landslide, another one in Rodriguez, Rizal due to strong currents, and one more in Naic, Cavite due to a vehicular accident. Further, the OCD said four persons also remained missing: two in Baguio and one in Atok, Benguet due to separate landslides, and one in Batangas. A total of 2,270,862 individuals from 646,676 families were affected by the torrential rains from the severe weather disturbances across 10 regions namely Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), National Capital Region (NCR), Ilocos (Region 1), Cagayan Valley (Region 2), Central Luzon (Region 3), Calabarzon (Region 4A), Mimaropa (Region 4B), Bicol (Region 5), Western Visayas (Region 6), and Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9). The widespread impact has also forced 94,997 individuals or 26,174 families to seek temporary shelter in 919 active evacuation centers. OCD spokesperson Junie Castillo said the hardest-hit areas were spread across several regions, with La Union and Pangasinan bearing the brunt in Ilocos Region. “If we are talking about the areas, Region 1 is considered the hardest hit, particularly the provinces of La Union and Pangasinan,” Castillo said. CAR was also heavily affected, particularly Baguio City and Benguet, where landslides have caused most of the reported deaths and injuries in the latest figures. In Central Luzon, Castillo identified Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan and Nueva Ecija among the badly affected areas. The effects of the weather disturbances have also reached Calabarzon and Metro Manila. Damage Meanwhile, the disasters also damaged 684 houses, of which, 639 were partially damaged while 45 were totally destroyed. Infrastructure losses ballooned to P1.456 billion while damage to agriculture was estimated at P135.33 million. The government has so far provided P73.52 million in assistance to affected communities. ‘Prepare for more rains’ Castillo said response agencies were preparing for more rains even if conditions were expected to improve temporarily. “According to PAGASA, the weather will calm down a little, but by the weekend, the rains will return,” he said. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) has continued to monitor the weather situation as habagat remains capable of bringing heavy rains over parts of the country. Castillo stressed that residents should not let the temporary improvement in weather lead to complacency. “For our fellow Filipinos, it is very important that we remain prepared and alert while the response agencies continue to stand by,” he said. “In fact, all response clusters are on standby, aside from those already deployed for response operations, because we are looking at more rain in the coming days,” Castillo added.

Philippine fintech workforce needs deeper AI, cybersecurity skills—ADB report. The Philippines needs to deepen its pool of advanced financial technology (fintech) talent, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity, despite having an established information technology and business process management (IT-BPM) sector and a large base of English-proficient workers, according to a joint report by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Global Fintech Institute (GFI). The report, “Bridging the Divide: An ASEAN Fintech Skills Framework for Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Vietnam,” published last Monday, Aug. 10, found persistent skills gaps across the four Southeast Asian economies covered by the study. Prepared by Singapore-headquartered think tank GFI with support from the Manila-based ADB, the study estimated an overall technical skills gap of 48 percent and a soft skills gap of 46 percent across Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Vietnam. For the Philippines, the report said the country could build on its existing service-sector and IT-BPM workforce as it shifts toward more advanced technical competencies. While the Philippines benefits from a strong IT-BPM sector and English-proficient talent, the report pointed to shortages in advanced technical fields such as AI and cybersecurity. The skills shortage comes as the Philippines rapidly adopts digital financial services. The share of digital payment transactions in total monthly retail payments rose to 52.8 percent in 2023 from 42.1 percent in 2022, exceeding the target under the Digital Payments Transformation Roadmap. Despite this progress, the Philippines was assessed at only a “developing” proficiency level in digital payments, regulatory technology (RegTech), cybersecurity, digital lending, and AI-enabled services. The report identified AI-enabled services as the country’s most critical technical gap, while digital lending was given greater priority in the Philippines and Vietnam than in Singapore. The country also received a “basic” assessment for technology and infrastructure awareness, with infrastructure gaps limiting proficiency and practical application. Core financial services, regulatory and compliance, risk and security, and fintech and digital innovation knowledge were all assessed at the “developing” level. The gaps are already affecting businesses, with 88 percent of Philippine respondents saying skills shortages have a high impact on their organizations’ ability to meet business objectives. Another 88 percent considered addressing the skills gap an immediate priority. Organizations in the Philippines and Singapore more often identified innovation and development as areas affected by skills shortages, while those in Indonesia and Vietnam more frequently pointed to risk and compliance. Meanwhile, the Philippines had 13 fintech-related programs in the study’s sample, consisting of government digital and cybersecurity courses, a small number of academic programs, and private boot camps. The report described the country’s training portfolio as fairly advanced, with a strong focus on foundational and intermediate digital skills, although fintech specialization remains limited. Across the four economies, the report found that technical expertise alone is insufficient, underscoring the need to combine it with soft skills and industry knowledge. Under its proposed Technical Skills, Soft Skills, and Industry Knowledge (TSI) framework, technical skills cover competencies required to develop and secure fintech products, while soft skills include problem-solving, communication, collaboration, and leadership. Industry knowledge covers financial services, regulation, risk, and market context. The report said employers expect technical expertise to be accompanied by financial services understanding and the ability to work across business and technology functions. Digital payments, RegTech, cybersecurity, digital lending, and AI-enabled services emerged as priority technical domains across the four markets. At the regional level, the report recommended developing more structured cross-border mobility pathways, including a possible digital skills passport or comparable credentialing mechanism, alongside practitioner-led certifications validated by the industry and, where appropriate, informed by regulators. For emerging markets (EMs) like the Philippines, the report also pointed to public-private partnerships (PPPs) as a means of providing practice-oriented training and exposing workers to real-world fintech applications and regulatory requirements. PPPs with universities and training providers were identified by 61 percent of surveyed businesses as the most effective policy intervention for closing skills gaps. Government-led initiatives such as the Philippines’ AI Academy could also support the transition of workers into AI-related roles and help address shortages in AI and cybersecurity skills. The report said fintech-related training across the four markets remains uneven in depth and specialization, with the Philippines, Indonesia, and Vietnam generally having programs concentrated on foundational digital skills, general information and communications technology (ICT), or a smaller number of institutions compared with Singapore. The findings were based partly on a September 2025 survey of 100 middle- to senior-level fintech professionals, with 25 respondents each from Indonesia, the Philippines, Singapore, and Vietnam. The report noted that the country-level findings indicate general trends rather than definitive results due to the small sample size. - Danielle T. Bayani

Filinvest Land profit improves on strong RFO sales, mall revenues. Filinvest Land Inc. (FLI), the listed property development arm of the Gotianun Group, reported a four-percent improvement in consolidated net income to ₱2.21 billion in the first half of 2026 on the back of gains in both property sales and rental operations. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, Aug. 11, FLI said total consolidated revenues were 2.9 percent higher at ₱12.57 billion compared with the same period last year, highlighting the enduring strength of the company’s diversified portfolio, disciplined execution, and expanding recurring income streams. FLI said the standout highlight of the period was the strong rebound in sales activity during the first half, with total reservation sales surging by 50 percent year-on-year to ₱12.5 billion. Momentum culminated in June, which recorded an impressive ₱3.7 billion—the company’s highest monthly reservation level since 2018. This growth was largely spearheaded by ready-for-occupancy (RFO) sales, which totaled ₱6.8 billion in the first half alone. Real estate revenues increased 3.3 percent to ₱7.72 billion, supported by the company’s strategic focus on monetizing RFO inventory and successfully answering buyers’ preferences for immediately available properties. “Our first-half results demonstrate Filinvest Land’s ability to translate demand into earnings through a disciplined, diversified business model,” said FLI President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Tristan Las Marias. He noted, “The strong pickup in reservation sales, particularly in RFO, reflects both improving buyer activity and the strength of our product offering across key markets.” Las Marias added, “At the same time, our leasing and recurring income businesses continue to provide stability and resilience, giving us a balanced platform for growth. As market conditions evolve, we remain focused on execution, capital efficiency, and capturing demand across our residential, commercial, and industrial segments.” The retail mall business sustained its robust momentum, with leasing revenues rising 12 percent to ₱1.47 billion as targeted asset enhancement initiatives and healthy tenant engagement successfully lifted mall occupancy to 81 percent. Meanwhile, office leasing revenues grew 2.4 percent to ₱2.54 billion, supported by an exceptional 100-percent renewal rate for all second-quarter lease expiries, underscoring the enduring reliability of FLI’s office portfolio. Complementing these gains, the industrial segment continues to capture robust demand, particularly through the 33-hectare (ha) mega lots at the Filinvest Innovation Park-New Clark City (FIP-NCC), as corporate occupiers aggressively secure strategic logistics and manufacturing hubs. - James A. Loyola

Eala projected 17th seed at Cincinnati Open. Alex Eala is expected to make the most out of the remaining days before she sees action again in the Cincinnati Open in Ohio which fires off on Thursday, Aug. 13. Barring any changes and last-minute pullouts, the 21-year-old is projected to be seeded 17th based on the latest player list from the organizers. According to tournament organizers, the singles draw features 96 players, with the 32 seeded players receiving first-round byes. All top 10 players except for world No. 6 Karolina Muchova are competing in the said WTA 1000 tournament, which serves as a prelude to the US Open slated late this month. Muchova, meanwhile, withdrew from the tournament after undergoing an unspecified surgery shortly following her runner-up finish at the Wimbledon Championships. Other notable names unable to compete with various continuing injuries and recoveries are 2025 finalist Jasmine Paolini, Hailey Baptiste and Victoria Mboko. The projected top 10 seeded players are world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka, Australian Open winner Elena Rybakina, 2024 US Open finalist Jessica Pegula, two-time Grand Slam champion Coco Gauff, French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, six-time Grand Slam winner Iga Swiatek, two-time Grand Slam finalist Amanda Anisimova, 2020 Tokyo Games bronze medalist Elina Svitolina and Wimbledon semifinalist Marta Kostyuk. Currently ranked No. 20 in the world, Eala is expected to ride on the momentum of her breakthrough WTA Tour title at the Mubadala DC Open last week, followed by a fourth-round finish at the WTA 1000 National Bank Open where she lost to seasoned player Belinda Bencic, 4-6, 0-6. Fatigue may have caught up with Eala after she had only a few days to recover between the DC Open and the National Bank Open, following a rain-delayed final against Jessica Pegula.

Lepanto profit more than doubles as gold, silver prices surge. Yap-led Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co. more than doubled its consolidated net income to ₱1.59 billion in the first half of 2026 from the ₱771 million earned in the same period last year as gold and silver prices surged in the world market. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, Aug. 11, the firm said it produced 10,931 ounces (oz) of gold and 21,346 oz of silver during the first six months of the year, resulting in a 47-percent jump in consolidated gross revenues to ₱3.24 billion from ₱2.2 billion in the same period last year. The average gold price surged to $4,684.40 per ounce (oz) from $3,084.80 an oz, while the silver price more than doubled to an average of $80.66 per oz from $32.94 per oz last year. The peso also weakened to ₱59.97 from ₱57.06 to the United States (US) dollar, further boosting revenues. “We continue to produce from the Victoria and Teresa orebodies. Efforts to further improve productivity and metal recoveries through equipment upgrades or rehabilitation continue. There are five active rigs drilling for both grade control and exploration with encouraging results,” Lepanto said. Last July 30, Lepanto and subsidiary Far Southeast Gold Resources Inc. (FSGRI) executed a memorandum of agreement (MOA) with the indigenous peoples (IPs) of Mankayan ancestral domain, signifying the granting to Lepanto and FSGRI of free and prior informed consent (FPIC) by the host indigenous cultural communities (ICCs)/IPs for the renewal of MPSA 001-90-CAR. The MOA will have a term of 25 years and was signed with the municipal mayor of Mankayan, Benguet province and the duly elected elders or leaders of each of the 12 barangays of Mankayan town, and witnessed by other local government unit (LGU) officials of Mankayan and representatives from the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP) and the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB). The MOA will be submitted to the NCIP for approval, which will be in the form of a certification precondition that, in turn, will be submitted to the MGB for the renewal of MPSA 001. - James A. Loyola

Mercado says PBBM’s directives top priority as he takes DOH helm. Newly appointed Department of Health (DOH) Secretary Dr. Edwin Mercado said on Tuesday, Aug. 11, that his immediate priority is to ensure that the agency is fully aligned and ready to carry out President Marcos’ directives. “The President’s directives are clear, and our immediate priority is to ensure that we are fully aligned and ready to carry out his instructions,” Mercado said in a statement. According to Mercado, he would first meet with newly appointed Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Dr. Beverly Lorraine Ho to discuss their shared priorities. “I will first meet with Dr. Bev to discuss our shared priorities. We will provide further updates once we have settled into our new roles,” he said. President Marcos appointed Mercado as the new DOH chief following the resignation of Dr. Jose “Brix” Pujalte. Mercado previously served as PhilHealth president and CEO before his appointment to the health department. Ho, meanwhile, was named as Mercado’s successor at the state health insurer. Mercado welcomed Ho’s appointment, describing her as a seasoned public health expert who began her career at PhilHealth. “She is a seasoned public health expert that started her career in PhilHealth, and we are excited to have her back - this time at its helm,” Mercado said. Likewise, Mercado expressed gratitude to the Chief Executive for his appointment. “I am grateful to the President for his continued trust in me,” he said. He also thanked Pujalte for his service as health secretary. “I would like to sincerely thank Dr. Jose ‘Brix’ Pujalte for his dedicated service and wish him continued success in his future pursuits,” Mercado said. On Aug. 10, Marcos named Mercado as the new DOH chief, succeeding Pujalte. Pujalte was appointed to lead the health department in July after Teodoro Herbosa left the post.

ACEN profit surges 411% to ₱3.9 billion on stronger energy sales. Ayala-led ACEN Corp. posted a more than fivefold increase in net income during the first half of 2026, driven by stronger energy sales and improved performance across its domestic and international renewable energy (RE) portfolio. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, Aug. 11, ACEN reported that its net income during the first half of the year surged 411 percent to ₱3.9 billion from ₱763 million in the same period in 2025. Overall earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) also jumped 40 percent to ₱14.7 billion. “ACEN’s performance in the first half of 2026 underscores our recovery from the challenges of the previous year while reflecting the company’s transition into a phase of measured growth,” ACEN President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Eric Francia said. “Amid a continually uncertain environment, our priorities remain clear—protecting our balance sheet, growing our contracted energy sales, and expanding our energy storage asset base,” Francia added. From January to July, attributable generation from its RE portfolio rose 21 percent to 4,024 gigawatt-hours (GWh), driven by new assets across its markets. Its attributable renewables capacity now stands at 7,517 megawatts (MW), after its battery energy storage projects in the Philippines—which have about 775 MW/1,660 megawatt-hours (MWh) of capacity—broke ground. Domestic revenues likewise increased 41 percent to ₱23.6 billion, as higher contracted energy sales from its growing retail electricity supply (RES) business drove earnings. During the period, ACEN RES increased its portfolio to 587 MW, while its 160-MW mid-merit contract with Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) also contributed to the company’s Philippine revenues. Its local RE generation grew 17 percent to 1,091 GWh, as its Pagudpud and Capa 2 wind projects in Ilocos Norte province delivered improved generation. Its operations in Australia likewise improved on contributions from its Stubbo solar operations and reduced grid curtailment at New England solar 1 project. Its battery energy storage project is expected to become fully operational by the end of the year, while its 102-megawatt-direct-current (MWdc) Jinbi solar phase 1 is targeted for completion by late 2028. ACEN India’s generation stood at 476 GWh, factoring in the recently commissioned 153-MW Maharashtra hybrid project. It is expected to complete four RE developments by end-2027, including the 350-MW Tejorupa solar, 120-MW Bijapur wind, 389-MW Sheo 1 hybrid, and 399-MW Sheo 2 hybrid projects. Its attributable output in Mekong also increased 19 percent to 996 GWh, following the contribution of Monsoon wind in Laos and better solar resource conditions. Indonesia saw marginal growth of six percent over the six-month period. ACEN expects the 40-MW Salak unit 7 expansion to become operational by next year. Other international markets saw a 69-percent spike in attributable output to 196 GWh. As the company saw growing demand for indigenous renewables, ACEN Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Jonathan Beck said, “We intend to benefit from this growth while maintaining a prudent, financially disciplined path forward, including continued focus on cost management across all our businesses.” - Gabriell Christel Galang

PNP warns of possible habagat effect disinformation drive on social media. The Philippine National Police (PNP) warned the public, particularly netizens, to be wary of the photos and videos on social media, saying some of them could be old and fake that are deliberately posted for disinformation drives. Issues surrounding flood control have been a very sensitive topic for Filipinos over massive corruption involving projects that were allegedly turned as a milking cow of ranking government officials. And some of these fake and old images and videos are allegedly being exploited to direct public anger towards certain personalities. For instance, Deputy Speaker Paolo Ortega V of La Union said there were efforts to use misleading photos and videos to portray the alleged massive flooding in his home province. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr. urged the public to verify information first before sharing it to avoid causing fear and panic in communities already affected by heavy rains and flooding as some of the images and videos circulating online may be fake, altered, or taken from previous weather disturbances. “A number of kababayan need assistance and accurate information as a result of this calamity. This should be the time for compassion and bayanihan, not the time for any motive driven anger or any selfish interest,” said Nartatez. “Let us be discerning and cautious. Not everything we see online is true,” he added. The PNP warning came as heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon flooded parts of Metro Manila and other provinces in Luzon over the weekend. The bad weather prompted the suspension of classes and government work in affected areas. Nartatez said the public should be careful when encountering posts that claim to show the latest situation in areas hit by habagat. He warned that the circulation of misleading information can create a distorted picture of the situation on the ground, and may also cause unnecessary alarm among residents and make it harder for the public to distinguish actual warnings and advisories from false reports. Nartatez reminded the public to rely on information released by government agencies and authorities when checking the weather situation, forecasts, and the effects of habagat.

Robin Padilla wants up to 20 years jail for gov't personnel who lie in probes. Senator Robinhood Padilla has filed a bill seeking stiffer penalties for government personnel who knowingly provide false statements or fabricated evidence during congressional inquiries. Senate Bill No. 610, or the proposed “Truthful Congressional Inquiry Act,” would impose up to 10 years in prison on government personnel who make untruthful statements or present fabricated evidence involving material facts in congressional investigations into specified serious offenses. The penalty would rise to up to 20 years if the offender is from agencies including the Armed Forces of the Philippines, Philippine National Police, Philippine Coast Guard, Bureau of Fire Protection, Bureau of Corrections, National Bureau of Investigation, and Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency, among others. The bill also proposes a fine of up to P3 million, perpetual disqualification from holding elective or appointive government positions, and restrictions on eligibility for executive clemency. Padilla said tougher penalties were needed because Congress relies on accurate information when crafting laws and conducting oversight. “Congress relies on factual and accurate information in crafting laws and exercising its oversight functions. Kapag nagsinungaling o gumawa ng pekeng ebidensya ang isang kawani ng gobyerno sa harap ng Kongreso, hindi lamang ang mga mambabatas ang nililinlang—ang taumbayan mismo ang nililinlang (When a government employee lies or fabricates evidence before Congress, it is not only the lawmakers who are being deceived—the Filipino people themselves are being deceived),” Padilla said. Existing laws already penalize perjury and false testimony, but Padilla said government personnel who lie during congressional proceedings should face stronger deterrents because false information could affect legislation, oversight and the public interest. “Kung humihingi tayo ng katotohanan sa ordinaryong mamamayan, higit nating dapat itong hingin sa mga taong pinapasahod ng bayan. Walang puwang ang kasinungalingan at gawa-gawang ebidensya sa isang imbestigasyong ang layunin ay malaman ang katotohanan (If we demand the truth from ordinary citizens, then we should demand it even more from those paid by the people. There is no place for lies and fabricated evidence in an investigation whose purpose is to uncover the truth),” Padilla said. The bill seeks to strengthen accountability among government personnel and protect the integrity of congressional investigations.

AyalaLand Logistics profit plunges on weaker industrial lot sales, commercial leasing. AyalaLand Logistics Holdings Corp. (ALLHC) reported that its profit continued to drop, falling 89.5 percent to ₱11 million in the first half of 2026 from ₱105 million in the same period last year due to lower industrial lot sales and commercial leasing revenues. Based on its disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, Aug. 11, consolidated revenues declined 11 percent to ₱1.6 billion from the ₱1.8 billion registered in the same period last year, supported by continued growth in its industrial leasing businesses. Industrial lot sales dropped 44 percent to ₱489 million during the first six months of 2026 from ₱1.8 billion in the same period last year. “Customer interest in ALLHC’s technopark developments remained evident, with sales reservations reaching ₱791 million, up 11 percent year-on-year, despite the prevailing market environment,” the company said. It noted, “These reservations provide visibility for future revenue recognition as payment milestones are achieved.” ALLHC’s leasing businesses generated ₱1.1 billion in total revenues, a 13-percent increase year-on-year, driven by higher contributions from the company’s warehouse and cold storage facilities. Warehouse leasing revenues increased nine percent year-on-year to ₱391 million as occupancy across the portfolio continued to improve. Cold storage revenues nearly doubled to ₱243 million, up 99 percent year-on-year, due to higher utilization across most facilities. However, commercial leasing revenues declined six percent year-on-year to ₱438 million, reflecting softer occupancy during the period. ALLHC is expanding its cold storage capacity by about 14,000 pallets to over 40,000 pallets by the end of the year. In an earlier interview, ALLHC Chief Operating Officer (COO) Patrick John C. Avila said they have already completed two facilities this year, Artico Sta. Rosa in Laguna province and Artico Consolacion in Cebu province, with a combined capacity of 9,000 pallets. “We still have ongoing construction [or a third facility] in Cavite. We’re still working on that. The intention is [to complete it in] the latter part of this year,” he said, adding that this facility in Vermosa estate will have a capacity of 5,000 pallets. Avila noted that while they continue to work on their expansion plans, “the focus right now, because we already have nine operating cold storage facilities, the focus is to stabilize the operations, the occupancies.” ALLHC is also expanding its dry warehouse business and has just opened a new facility in Pampanga Technopark called ALogis Mabalacat, which has a gross leasable area of 25,700 square meters (sqm). This brings the ALogis chain’s total portfolio size to 380,000 sqm. - James A. Loyola

DHSUD implements housing loan amortization in areas affected by 'habagat'. The Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) has ordered a moratorium on housing loan amortizations for qualified beneficiaries in areas affected by widespread flooding and other adverse effects of the weather disturbances in the past days. DHSUD Secretary Jose Ramon Aliling said the moratorium will cover qualified member-beneficiaries of the National Housing Authority (NHA), Social Housing Finance Corporation (SHFC), and the National Home Mortgage Finance Corporation (NHMFC). But he said the move is subject to the respective policies and guidelines of key shelter agencies. “Each of the key shelter agencies will soon be coming out with their respective guidelines on the coverage of the moratorium and steps on how members can avail of it,” said Aliling. Earlier, President Marcos ordered all government agencies to ensure that assistance reaches all residents affected by the heavy rains, particularly those in far-flung communities. The moratorium on housing loan amortizations, according to Aliling, is in compliance with Marcos’ order, adding that DHSUD Regional Offices in affected areas were tasked to remain in close coordination with local government units and other agencies to determine the housing needs of affected families. “The Regional Offices were also instructed to give particular attention to communities in danger zones,” said Aliling. Based on the latest data of the Office of Ciivl Defense, more than 646,000 families composed of over 2.2 million people in 10 regions were affected by the series of weather disturbances that hit the country in the past days. More than 26,000 families have been staying in evacuation centers while a total of 684 houses were either partially or totally damaged.

Woman arrested with P340K shabu in Sta. Cruz. A 37-year-old woman listed as a high-value individual (HVI) was arrested after police allegedly recovered around 50 grams of suspected shabu during an operation in Sta. Cruz, Manila, on Sunday night, Aug. 9. The suspect, identified as Rose Hermosura, was arrested at around 10:30 p.m. along Rizal Avenue near the corner of Tambunting Street in Barangay 374, according to the Sta. Cruz Police Station’s Station Drug Enforcement Unit (SDEU). Police said the operation stemmed from a tip received by the station’s Tactical Operation Center about a woman allegedly involved in illegal drug activity in the area. SDEU personnel were dispatched to verify the information, which resulted in Hermosura’s arrest. Three heat-sealed transparent sachets containing a white crystalline substance believed to be shabu were allegedly recovered from her. Police estimated the total weight of the suspected drugs at around 50 grams, with an estimated street value of P340,000. A yellow-and-cream paper bag was also reportedly confiscated during the operation. Police said Hermosura was informed of the reason for her arrest and her constitutional rights in a language she understood. She reportedly chose to remain silent. Hermosura is currently detained at the Sta. Cruz Police Station custodial facility while police prepare the necessary documents for the filing of a case for violation of Section 11, Article II of Republic Act 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002. The confiscated substances will undergo the required examination and documentation as part of the investigation.

Bantay Bata member electrocuted, killed in Batangas mishap. LOBO, Batangas- A 23-year-old Bantay Dagat member died after he was electrocuted while assisting Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) personnel on Monday afternoon, August 10, in Barangay Sawang. The victim was identified as Chris, 23, and a resident of Barangay Lagadlarin, Lobo, Batangas. Reports said that, at around 1:25 p.m., the victim was assisting personnel of the Philippine Coast Guard stationed in Lobo, Batangas, in pulling their boat toward the shoreline using an electric winch. Then he suddenly experienced involuntary body movements and was believed to have been electrocuted through contact with the winch line. The Lobo Coast Guard rendered first aid to the victim and later took him to Lobo Municipal Hospital where he was declared dead on arrival.

2027 confidential, intelligence funds lower by 8.8%--DBM. The sought P10.733 billion confidential and intelligence funds (CIFs) under the proposed P7.2-trillion National Expenditure Program (NEP) for 2027 is lower by 8.8 percent compared to the current 2026 budget. Thus, bared Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Acting Secretary Kim Robert de Leon in a press conference following the ceremonial turnover of the 2027 NEP at the House of Representatives on Tuesday morning, Aug. 11. "We wish to note that this P10.773 billion in combined [CIFs] is lower from the 2026 GAA level for [CIFs] of P11.818 billion, or lower by 8.8 percent," De Leon said in response to a reporter's query. The GAA or General Appropriations Act refers to the enacted budget this year, worth P6.793 trillion. De Leon said the P10.773 billion is broken down into P4.368 billion in confidential funds, P6.405 billion in intelligence funds. "And we wish to reiterate that the use of confidential and intelligence funds remain subject to existing budgeting, utilization, liquidation, and auditing rules to ensure accountability and that the funds are used solely for their respective services," the DBM chief said. He said the CIF recipients under the 2027 NEP were comparable to the agencies and departments that received the secret funds this year. He noted that the Philippine National Police (PNP) had a "slight increase" in proposed CIF under the 2027 spending plan. "Pero definitely ito po ay mas mababa pa rin doon sa...2026 level ng ating [CIF]," said De Leon. (But definitely this is still lower than the 2026 level of our [CIF].) "Tanging yung mga ahensya na legally authorized na magkaroon ng confidential and intelligence functions ang mayroong [CIF] under the 2027 [NEP], he stressed. (Only agencies legally authorized to have confidential and intelligence functions have [CIF] under the 2027 [NEP].)

Dredging ops in Metro Manila 'effective' so far, but still not enough — Marcos. President Marcos said dredging operations across major rivers, esteros, and drainage networks in Metro Manila have been effective so far, but noted that more needs to be done. During his inspection of the high-vacuum self-priming drainage trailer pump in Barangay Zapote, Las Piñas City, on Tuesday, Aug. 11, Marcos said the dredging operations that started this year appeared to have had an effect. He noted that flooding was not as severe as before, when the water would reach chest level. "So, effective naman ang ating ginagawa ngunit alam naman natin kulang pa rin ‘yan. Marami pa rin tayong kailangan gawin (So, what we are doing is proving to be effective, but we know that it is still not enough. There is still a lot that we need to do)," Marcos said in an interview during the inspection. The President further noted that the government had only recently resumed dredging operations after a 12-year moratorium, during which rivers and spillways became increasingly shallow. Ngunit mukha namang effective yung ating nagawa na, na nasimulan nitong taon na ito. Hindi natin titigilan hanggang matapos ‘yan. Ang dredging talagang walang tigil ‘yan, tuluy-tuloy ‘yan (But what we’ve done so far seems to be effective, especially the work we started this year. We won’t stop until it’s finished. The dredging, in particular, will continue nonstop)," he said. During the inspection, Marcos witnessed the extraction of water from the Alido River into the Zapote River using the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) deployed drainage pump. The high-vacuum self-priming drainage trailer pump is aimed at reducing water levels in the Alido River and helping mitigate flooding in surrounding areas. Revisit stalled spillway plan Marcos said he has instructed the DPWH to revisit the spillway plans which have been stalled for more than 10 years. The President cited the spillway in Las Piñas which needs to be finished, saying "that plan has been stalled for far too long." He also underscored that completing the spillway in the city would also address flooding in the National Capital Region (NCR). "That plan has been in the works for – I don't know, more than 10 years. Pero (But) for some whatever reason, hindi natin nabuo at ngayon kailangan gagawin na natin (we were not able to complete it but now, we really need to)," Marcos added. "So, I have given instructions to Secretary Vince na tingnan na muna natin, balikan na natin ang mga plano. Tingnan natin kung may kailangang palitan. But whatever it is, kung anong kailangan gawin, kailangan tapusin na natin. Ilagay na natin yung spillway. Malaking, malaking bagay ‘yan para sa pagbabaha ng NCR (to take a look at it first and revisit the plans. Let’s see if there’s anything that needs to be changed. But whatever it is, whatever needs to be done, we need to get it finished. Let’s build the spillway. That would make a huge, huge difference in addressing flooding in the NCR)," Marcos said. 'Improper waste disposal can cause enormous damage' Marcos has called on local government units (LGU), residents, and others involved to be responsible in the disposal of garbage, citing the recent incident where drainage canals were completely filled with garbage amid the heavy rains. "Ang isa pang issue na nakita natin na nangyari ay yung nagbabaan yung sa Parañaque lalo – ay yung nagbabaan ang basura. Nakita ninyo yung mga picture na punung-puno yung kanal, punung-puno ng basura na hindi naman galing sa Parañaque, galing sa ibang lugar yun (Another issue we noticed was the amount of trash that came down, particularly in Parañaque. You saw the pictures—the drainage canals were completely filled with garbage. And that garbage didn’t even come from Parañaque; it came from other areas)," Marcos said. "Pero dahil nabuksan na yung ating mga kanal, lahat doon napasok, nasabayan pa ng high tide kaya naipit yung mga basura doon (But because our drainage canals had already been opened, all of that garbage flowed into them, and the high tide made the situation worse, causing the trash to get trapped there)," Marcos added. "Kaya’t nananawagan kami sa lahat ng involved, ang ating mga local government unit, ang ating lahat ng mamamayang Pilipino, mag-ingat po kayo dahil ang laking pinsala ang nangyayari kapag ‘yung basura natin ay hindi maganda ang pagtapon at dahil kung saan-saan na lang nilalagay (That’s why we are calling on everyone involved, our local government units, and all our fellow Filipinos—to be careful because improper waste disposal and simply throwing garbage wherever we want can cause enormous damage)," the President further said. He assured the public that the government will continue with its waste-to-energy program, which involves collecting the garbage, processing it, and converting it into electricity. The Chief Executive emphasized that it will be a very significant development once it is completed. He also said that the flood-control efforts and related projects, including dredging will continue. "Pati kasama ang LGU at ang LGU ay nakakasama na rin natin sa dredging at makikita natin ang effect na ito (We are also working together with the LGUs, which are now participating in the dredging efforts, and we can already see the impact)," he said. "Kaya kahit may baha pa nang kaunti ay malaki ang binawas, hindi na ganoon kalalim, una-una. Pangalawa, mas mabilis mawala yung tubig dahil nga nabuksan na natin ang ating mga kanal (So even though there is still some flooding, the situation has improved significantly. First, the floodwater is no longer as deep. Second, the water recedes much faster because we have already opened up our drainage canals)," he added.

Sri Lanka’s foreign minister reaffirms investment cooperation during visit to PHIVIDEC Industrial Estate. Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath of Sri Lanka visited the PHIVIDEC Industrial Estate in Misamis Oriental on 30 July 2026 as part of his official trip to the Mindanao region. The visit underscored Sri Lanka’s commitment to strengthening economic cooperation with the Philippines and provided the Minister an opportunity to witness firsthand the progress of Sri Lankan investments in the country, particularly those of Haycarb PLC. Minister Herath was accompanied by Sri Lanka’s Ambassador to the Philippines, Dr. Chanaka Talpahewa; Embassy Attaché/Consular Officer Chaturi Kalpana; and Honorary Consul for Mindanao William Chen. The visit coincided with the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Sri Lanka and the Philippines—a milestone year that has also marked the first-ever Sri Lankan investments in the Philippines. The delegation was warmly received by Atty. Joseph Bernedo, Administrator of PHIVIDEC; Hon. Atty. Nadya Emano-Maniwan, Mayor of Tagoloan; Ms. Ellen Kionisala of the Board of Investments; senior government and local officials; PHIVIDEC staff; and representatives of Haycarb and Jaindi Exports. They were briefed on the estate’s facilities and services, as well as the ongoing investments of the two Sri Lankan companies. Discussions highlighted opportunities to further expand trade, investment, and commercial cooperation between the two nations. Speaking during the visit, Minister Herath emphasized: “The Government of Sri Lanka attaches great importance to supporting and protecting the investments made by Sri Lankan companies overseas. This visit has given us the opportunity to see firsthand the excellent facilities and investor-friendly environment at the PHIVIDEC Industrial Estate. We hope this will encourage many more Sri Lankan businesses to explore investment opportunities in the Philippines and contribute to even stronger economic ties between our two countries.” The delegation welcomed the progress of Haycarb PLC, whose activated carbon manufacturing facility is under construction at PHIVIDEC. While the factory’s inauguration was initially hoped to coincide with the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations, construction has been delayed due to global economic challenges. Once completed, the facility will represent the first Sri Lankan manufacturing investment in the Philippines and a significant milestone in bilateral economic relations. Jaindi Exports was also commended for its forthcoming project, now in the final stages of approval and expected to begin construction soon. The decision of a second Sri Lankan company to invest in PHIVIDEC reflects growing confidence in the Philippines as an investment destination and demonstrates the estate’s appeal to international investors. Together, the two projects represent an estimated initial investment of approximately US$20 million and are expected to generate over 150 direct jobs for the local community, alongside numerous indirect employment opportunities. They will also contribute to technology transfer, exports, and regional economic development. The delegation praised PHIVIDEC for its modern, investor-friendly environment and proactive support in facilitating foreign direct investment. With its strategic location, quality infrastructure, and efficient services, PHIVIDEC offers an excellent platform for international companies seeking to establish operations in the southern Philippines. Minister Herath expressed gratitude to Ambassador Talpahewa for his tireless efforts in advancing Sri Lankan investments in the Philippines, and extended appreciation to PHIVIDEC management, the Department of Foreign Affairs, the Board of Investments, and other government agencies whose cooperation has been instrumental in bringing these projects to fruition. The delegation visited the Haycarb site and the proposed site for Jaindi Exports, and to commemorate the occasion, Minister Herath and his team planted tree saplings on the Haycarb premises. As Sri Lanka and the Philippines celebrate 65 years of diplomatic relations, both countries reaffirm their commitment to expanding cooperation across diplomacy, trade, investment, tourism, education, and people-to-people exchanges. The establishment of Sri Lankan investments in the Philippines marks a new chapter in bilateral relations and lays the foundation for an even stronger partnership in the years ahead.

Low AI adoption in retail and in all Philippines to stunt GDP growth. Whie the hype surrounding AI is at an all time high, the Philippines is on the verge of missing out on massive economic gains, because as a nation, we have not learned to use artificial intelligence to our advantage. Both local and foreign studies show that the country’s sluggish adoption rate could severely stunt long-term gross domestic product (GDP) growth. A study by global management consulting firm Kearney estimates that robust AI adoption could add roughly $92 billion to the Philippine economy by 2030. Meanwhile, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) puts its own projections even higher, suggesting AI could unlock up to ₱2.6 trillion a year for the country. Yet, the gap between potential and reality remains vast. Hype vs. reality "But here’s the uncomfortable truth about AI adoption: real, value-creating adoption is still low; not just in retail, and not just in the Philippines," notes RJ Paculan, Innovation Strategist at TBWA\SMP. The issue isn't that enterprises aren't opening accounts or experimenting with the technology; it's that they aren't integrating it into their core operations. A 2025 McKinsey study highlights this exact friction point: while 88% of organizations use AI in some capacity, a mere seven percent have successfully scaled it across their business. In the local retail sector, the numbers are even more stark, falling far below the already conservative national average. According to a 2025 Gallup report, only 33 percent of retail employees use AI even a few times a year. To be fair, the Philippines isn't alone in this struggle. Globally, organizations are hitting a wall when it comes to turning pilots into profits. A 2025 MIT study revealed that a staggering 95 percent of Generative AI pilots deliver no measurable return on investment. "FOMO wearing a business suit" The problem is, most companies look at AI entirely wrong, treating it as a novel tool to study. "I have sat in countless meetings where the client opens with: 'Paolo, we need to do something with AI," says Paolo Broma, Innovation Lead at TBWA\SMP. "Do something with AI" is not a business objective. It’s FOMO wearing a business suit,” Broma points out. The bottomless rabbit hole Attempting to master AI is perhaps the deepest imaginable rabbit hole in human history. “Literally every week there’s a new tool, a new model, a major upgrade to an existing one. People feel that if they haven’t started, they’re too far behind to ever catch up — so they don’t start at all,” says Broma. But Paculan offers sober consolation: “The technology is New — and it will keep being new every single week. You will never feel fully caught up, and that’s fine; nobody is.” So the REAL question is, where DOES one begin with AI? To help local businesses bridge the gap between AI dabbling and harnessing AI as a game changing business solution, executives from TBWA\SMP will be discussing these concepts in depth at the upcoming National Retailers Conference and Expo, happening on Aug. 6 and 7 at the SMX Convention Center in Mall of Asia. TBWA\SMP innovation executives will give actionable advice on how businesses can start using AI to its full potential in their aptly titled talk “Where Do I Even Begin with AI?”

Aside from backwages, employers are mandated to remit SSS contributions of illegally dismissed employees -- SC. The Supreme Court (SC) has reminded employers that employees who are illegally dismissed are entitled not only to full backwages but also to the remittance of their Social Security System (SSS) contributions from the time they were dismissed until they are reinstated. In a decision written by Associate Justice Maria Filomena D. Singh, the SC pointed out that illegally dismissed employees are considered to have remained employed during the period covered by their backwages and are therefore entitled to the rights and benefits that would have accrued during that period. The SC cited Article 294 of the Labor Code which mandates that an employee who is illegally dismissed from employment is entitled to full backwages and other benefits. Citing its previous decisions, the SC said that illegally dismissed employees are deemed to have not left their employment, and, thus, they are entitled to all rights and privileges that accrue to them from the said employment. The reminder was made in its decision that denied the petition of Lopez Sugar Corporation (LSC). Four LSC employees – Romeo Perrin Jr., Eduardo Candelario, Leonito Franco and Rogelio Pabalan – were ordered reinstated to their former positions and paid their full backwages. After the ruling became final, Perrin and his group asked LSC to remit their SSS contributions for the period covered by their backwages so they could qualify for retirement benefits. However, LSC refused as it argued that under the SSS Act of 1997, its obligation to pay SSS contributions ended upon the employees’ separation from employment, regardless of whether their dismissal was legal or illegal. The Social Security Commission (SSC) rejected LSC’s position and ordered it to pay the contributions. The SSC ruled that because the employees were illegally dismissed, the employer-employee relationship was deemed to have continued during the period they were prevented from working. The Court of Appeals affirmed the SSC ruling. LSC elevated the case to the SC. In denying the petition, the SC ruled that LSC remained obligated to remit the employees’ SSS contributions for the period covered by their backwages. The SC said: “Here, there is no dispute that Perrin et al. were illegally dismissed, as ruled by the NLRC (National Labor Relations Commission) and affirmed by the CA and the Court (SC). Thus, they are deemed to have never left their employment. “Consequently, LSC's obligation to remit Perrin et al.' s social security contributions did not cease with respect to the period during which Perrin et al. were illegally dismissed. “Since LSC failed to remit Perin et al.'s social security contributions, LSC is liable to pay a penalty thereon of three percent (3%) per month from the date the contribution falls due until paid, pursuant to Section 22 of the Social Security Act of 1997. “Accordingly, the Petition for Review on Certiorari is denied. The Decision, dated Oct. 14, 2020, and the Resolution, dated April 26, 2022, of the Court of Appeals in CA-G.R. SP No. 158759 are affirmed.”

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. Click here to listen on Apple Podcasts or Spotify . For more, check out Sabine’s book “ The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response ”, and our Europe page.
